(default 47900, else any free port), bind?: "local" (this machine, default) | "lan" (the local network) | an IP address} → the open file's session: {session, link, url (invites: they carry the secret token), address, …}; sessions are per file, so other files' sessions go on (a session this file was in ends)

figcraft.label: Share with a join code
figcraft.params: {via?: "online" (default: the open file is kept on the server in Preferences, `pref.publishServer`, and the server hands out the codes) | "local" (this app hosts it for people on the same network; no server), access?: "edit" (default) | "view" (online only: which code `code` is), server? (online: another server's address, with ?key=… when it needs its key), name? (online: the file's name there), port?, bind?: "lan" (default) | "local" (this machine only) | an IP address (local)} → the open file's session as `collab.peers` gives it: `code` is what others type to join (`collab.join {code}`, the Join field), `link` an invite link. Local: at once, the code carries the host's IPv4 address, port and secret (K7M2Q-…, 20 symbols). Online: status "connecting" first; once live `code` is the server's (K7M-2QX-9TD) and `share` is {via, access, shared, editCode, viewCode, editLink, viewLink}: links made for others (the file's own links in `published` stay yours); `code` stays null when the server is older than join codes (give `share.editLink` / `share.viewLink` instead). Called again while shared: only switches which code `code` is (`access`). Called after `collab.stop` on a file that is still on the server: new links and codes for that same file (nothing is published twice). `collab.stop` stops sharing

figcraft.label: Stop live session

A file shared online with `collab.share` is different: its sharing stops → {ended: false, shared: false}: the links and codes others got are revoked on the server, whoever joined with them is disconnected at once (they keep their copy), and you stay in the file, which stays on the server, open only to you (`collab.share` shares it again with new codes; `collab.leave` leaves it there; `collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` with its owner token takes it off the server)

figcraft.label: Leave live session

(default: the file's name)} → status "connecting": the open file is uploaded as a new file and this tab syncs through the server; `collab.peers` then has `published: {server, file, name, edit, view, owner (published without a key: the owner token, shown once), expires (seconds since 1970, or null)}` and `hosting` (the server's operator, terms and idle expiry)

(when files on several servers have that id)} → {session, status: "connecting", document, alreadyOpen, file, server, name}: joins the file as its owner in a tab of its own (`collab.peers` tells when it's live; `collab.share` and `collab.stop` there start and stop its sharing); a file that is open already comes to the front instead (alreadyOpen: true)

The file stays on its server until it expires, and without its owner token it can't be managed from here again (`collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` takes it off the server instead)

figcraft.label: Recover online file
figcraft.params: {path (a recovery copy of one of your online files), file, server?, session, client, seq (who the app was in the file when the copy was written, and the server's last change it had: from the note beside the copy)} → {session, status: "connecting"}: joins the file again as its owner and keeps the copy until the file arrives. Then: the server has everything in the copy → nothing more; the copy has changes of yours the server never confirmed and nothing else changed there → they are applied on top as one edit ("Recovered changes", synced to everyone); anything else changed meanwhile → the copy opens beside the file as “<name> (recovered copy)”; the file can't be joined → the copy opens as an unsaved document. lightcraft.label: Face Model Downloads
lightcraft.params: {} → {running, downloads: [{id, state: running | done | installed | failed | cancelled, bytes, total, error, from}]} — also installs any download that has arrived; `installed` stays listed until `faces.models.downloadCancel` clears it

lightcraft.label: Cancel Face Model Download
lightcraft.params: {id} → {discarded} — stop a download, or delete a finished one that was not installed

lightcraft.label: Test Face Model
lightcraft.params: {id} → {ok, result: {loadMs, embedMs, dimension, checks}} — load an installed recognition model and check it gives sensible faces; needs the recognition runtime

lightcraft.label: Remove Face Model
lightcraft.params: {id} — delete an installed model

lightcraft.label: Choose Face Recognition Model
lightcraft.params: {id: installed recogniser | null}

lightcraft.label: Face Recognition On/Off
lightcraft.params: {enabled?: bool} (toggles when omitted)

lightcraft.label: Detect Faces
lightcraft.params: {ids?, apply?: bool (default true), score?: 0.6, nmsIou?: 0.3, maxFaces?} → {photos: [{id, faces: [{rect, score, landmarks}]}]}. Finds faces with the YuNet detector (download it first: `faces.models.download {id: "yunet-2023mar"}`) and, unless `apply` is false, adds them as unnamed face regions (one undo step), replacing earlier detections but never regions from XMP or ones you named; the sidecar is not touched

lightcraft.label: Face Models on the GPU
lightcraft.params: {cpuOnly?: bool} → {cpuOnly, detection, recognition}: where the face models run, each as {checking, device, why} (null until it is loaded). The GPU is used only after a background check shows it gives the CPU's results faster; `cpuOnly: true` keeps every face model on the CPU (Settings ▸ Faces), `false` checks the GPU again

lightcraft.label: Index Faces
lightcraft.params: {budgetMs?: 200, ids?: [photo ids to do first]} → {embedded, photosDone, pendingPhotos, indexedFaces, ms} — embed the faces in the library with the chosen recognition model, as many photos as fit in the time (at least one); call again until `pendingPhotos` is 0. `budgetMs: 0` only reports

lightcraft.label: Suggest Names for Faces
lightcraft.params: {ids?, threshold?, margin?, budgetMs?} → {photos: [{id, faces: [{index, suggestion: {name, score, runnerUp} | null, candidates: [{name, score}]}]}]} — who the unnamed faces in these photos might be, from the faces already named in the library. Only suggestions: nothing is named

lightcraft.label: Index Faces in the Background
lightcraft.params: {pace?: pause | light | normal | full} → {active, inFlight, pendingPhotos, indexedFaces, searchedPhotos, workers} — cheap to call every frame: takes in what the background workers have finished and gives them the next photos, as many at once as the pace allows (none when paused, one when light, half the machine's threads when normal, four fifths when full); inactive until face recognition is on in Settings with a model chosen

lightcraft.label: Evaluate Face Recognition
lightcraft.params: {budgetMs?: 0, burstSecs?: 5, margin?, thresholds?: [..], scope?: "visible"} → {queries, top1, sweep: [{threshold, suggested, correct, precision, recall}]} — leave-one-out over your named faces: each is ranked against the others (ignoring shots within burstSecs of it) to show how well the chosen model recognises people in *your* photos and which threshold to trust. Faces not yet embedded are done within budgetMs (`faces.index` does them all); counts only

lightcraft.label: Unnamed Faces
lightcraft.params: {limit?: 600} → {total, faces: [{photo, index, rect, view, suggestion: {name, score} | null}], ordered, ready} — the faces nobody has named; with recognition running, look-alikes are next to each other and a face the named ones recognise carries the name they suggest. `view` is the box to show the face by. Name them with `faces.nameFaces`

lightcraft.label: Name Faces
lightcraft.params: {faces: [{photo, index}], name} → {named, photos} — name (or, with a null or empty name, clear) many face regions as one undoable step; the sidecar is not touched

lightcraft.label: Faces of a Person
lightcraft.params: {name, more?: 120} → {name, total, confirmed: [{photo, index, rect}], more: [{photo, index, rect, score}], ready, pendingPhotos} — the faces named `name` across the library, and the unnamed faces that look most like them (best first, already embedded ones only, once recognition is on); confirm one with `faces.setName`

lightcraft.label: Name Face
lightcraft.params: {id?, index, name} — name a face region (null or empty clears it); undoable; the sidecar is not touched

lightcraft.label: Rename Person
lightcraft.params: {from, to, merge?: bool} → {faces, photos, from, to, merged} — give every in-library face of `from` the name `to` (trimmed, any capitalization), one undo step; refused when `to` is already someone else unless `merge` is true, which combines the two; the sidecar is not touched

lightcraft.label: Read Focus Points
lightcraft.params: {ids?, wait?: false} → {queued, running, last?: {total, done, found, none, unavailable, bytesRead, seconds, cancelled}} — read the camera's focus point for photos imported before it was read (Sony α1 and A7S III raws and JPEGs), from the few KB of each file that hold it, on a background job with a row in the activity stack. Without `ids`, every photo in the library not looked at yet; with `ids`, those photos, looked at again. Photos that have a point keep it. No undo step and no sidecar write. `wait: true` returns when all are read (scripts)

lightcraft.label: Read Focus Points in the Background
lightcraft.params: {pace?: pause | light | normal} → {active, running?: {done, total, found}, last?, lookedAt} — cheap to call every frame (the app does): takes in what the background focus-point reader has read and commits it in batches; reads nothing new while paused and rests between files when light. Starts the reader by itself once per library opening when photos are left to look at

lightcraft.label: Background Tasks
lightcraft.params: {} → {tasks: [{id, kind, label, done, total, unit: count|bytes|percent, detail, cancellable, cancelling, ageMs}]} — the long-running tasks in flight (imports, exports, preview builds, downloads, the face scan…), oldest first; total 0 = not known yet

lightcraft.label: Cancel Background Task
lightcraft.params: {id} | {all: true} → {cancelled: n} — ask a task (or every cancellable task) to stop; it stops at its next file or photo. An unknown id (it may have just finished) or a task that can't be cancelled is an error

photocraft.label: Move Action or Step
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?, "to":index}. Move a step within its action, or the action itself. to is the final zero-based index. Pending recorded steps can be moved.

photocraft.label: Get Action
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index} → {name, steps:[[id, params]…], disabled:[step…], dialogs:[step…], set:name|null, color:str} (steps is the shape file.automate.batch and droplets take; disabled lists the 0-based steps playback skips; dialogs the steps whose dialog Photoshop would show; set the action set from Load Actions; color is the Button Mode swatch, or empty)

photocraft.label: Stop Recording
photocraft.params: {} → {action, steps:count} (steps recorded since actions.record, queries and action-editing commands omitted)

photocraft.label: Play Action
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index, "from":step?} → {action, ran, failed?:{step, id, error}}. step and from are 0-based; steps switched off with actions.toggle are skipped. Stops at the first error (the command still returns ok, with failed set) and leaves one history step per step that ran. Nested calls are supported up to 16 levels; cycles are rejected. Recording stores a named call rather than its expanded commands. Each step is checked with Session::authorize when one is installed.

photocraft.label: Delete Action
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?} → {deleted:name} or {action, deletedStep, steps:count}. step is 0-based, including pending recorded steps. Whole-action deletion is refused while recording.

photocraft.label: Toggle Action Steps
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index, "step":index?, "enabled":bool?} → {action, disabled:[step…]}. Switch one 0-based step (including pending recorded steps) on or off for playback, Batch and droplets; omitted enabled flips it. Without step, switch every step: on unless all already are, or as enabled says.

photocraft.label: Rename Action
photocraft.params: {"action":name|index, "name":str} → {action, index}. The name must not be empty or whitespace-only and must be unique. Nested Play Action steps and the action's function key follow the rename.

photocraft.label: Set Action Color

vectorcraft.label: Document JSON
vectorcraft.params: {} → complete document model

vectorcraft.label: Units
vectorcraft.params: {units: "Points"|"Picas"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|"Centimeters"|"Pixels"|"Feet & Inches"|"Meters"|"Yards"|"Feet"} the document's units: every length the UI shows and reads (General)

vectorcraft.label: Ruler Origin
vectorcraft.params: {artboard?: index=0 (the active artboard, which artboard rulers measure from)} → {x, y} the rulers' zero point, in absolute document points

vectorcraft.label: Ruler Origin
vectorcraft.params: {x, y, artboard?: index=0} set the rulers' zero point in absolute document points: the document's with global rulers, that artboard's with artboard rulers (it moves with the artboard); art, guides and command coordinates stay in place

vectorcraft.label: Reset Ruler Origin
vectorcraft.params: {artboard?: index=0} reset the rulers' zero point to that artboard's top-left corner (with artboard rulers, that artboard's own zero point)

vectorcraft.label: Change to Global Rulers
vectorcraft.params: {global?: bool (default: toggle)} global rulers measure the whole document from one zero point; artboard rulers (a new document's) from the active artboard's top-left corner, or the zero point set for it. Saved with the document → {global}

vectorcraft.label: Drop Artwork
vectorcraft.params: {sourceDocument: uid, ids: [id…], grab: [x,y], at: [x,y]} copy 1–10000 editable source objects from an open document to the active document, preserving the grab point and clipboard, as one undo step

vectorcraft.label: Clear History
vectorcraft.params: {} remove every undo and redo step of the active document (the History panel menu's Clear History): the document stays as it is, and clearing is not an undo step → {cleared: the number of steps removed}

vectorcraft.label: Begin Undo Group
vectorcraft.params: {label?: string} until edit.undoGroup.end, the edits made in the active document are one undo step, named `label` (else after its first edit): for automation, such as MCP command_batch with `atomic` (#1163)

vectorcraft.label: End Undo Group
vectorcraft.params: {cancel?: bool} close the undo group: its edits stay one undo step or, with `cancel`, are undone

vectorcraft.label: Cut
vectorcraft.params: {} (the Artboard tool chosen: artboard.cut)

vectorcraft.label: Copy
vectorcraft.params: {} (the Artboard tool chosen: artboard.copy)

vectorcraft.label: Paste
vectorcraft.params: {center?: [x, y], dx?, dy?, swatchConflict?} paste centred on `center` (the app passes the view centre), else offset by dx/dy (default: the Paste Offset preference). Pasting brings the image blobs, symbols, patterns, global and spot swatches (with the tint swatches of the tints used), gradient swatches, graphic styles, character and paragraph styles and brushes the objects use; one of the same name that differs comes in renamed. swatchConflict, for a swatch whose name the document gives another colour (clipboard.conflicts): "merge" (default: the objects take the document's swatch) | "add" (the pasted swatch comes in renamed) | {name: "merge"|"add"}. With Paste Remembers Layers on (layer.pasteRemembersLayers), objects go back into the layers they came from (by name; made when missing). Artboards copied with artboard.copy come with their art, together right of the last artboard as they lay (the other paste commands but Paste on All Artboards: where they were), their art back in the layers it came from, and the Artboard tool, when chosen, selects them → {ids, artboard: the first new artboard's index or null, artboards: the new artboards' indices, added: resources added, merged: conflicts merged, renamed: [{kind, from, to}]}

vectorcraft.label: Paste in Front
vectorcraft.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (the active artboard: the objects go where they were on the artboard they were copied from, on this one)} paste in place just above the top selected object, or on top of the current layer when nothing is selected (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

vectorcraft.label: Paste in Back
vectorcraft.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (as edit.pasteInFront)} paste in place just below the bottom selected object, or at the bottom of the current layer when nothing is selected (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

vectorcraft.label: Paste in Place
vectorcraft.params: {swatchConflict?, artboard?: index (as edit.pasteInFront)} paste where the objects were copied (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

vectorcraft.label: Paste on All Artboards
vectorcraft.params: {swatchConflict?} paste a copy on every artboard at the offset the objects had to the artboard they were copied from (resources and layers as edit.paste) → {ids, added, merged, renamed}

vectorcraft.label: Clear
vectorcraft.params: {ids?} delete the objects `ids`, else the selection (fully selected objects and direct-selected anchors together, else ruler guides)

vectorcraft.label: Duplicate
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), dx?, dy?} duplicate the selection in place (offset optional)

vectorcraft.label: Clipboard as SVG
vectorcraft.params: {} → {svg} the copied objects as standalone SVG (null when the clipboard is empty)

vectorcraft.label: Load SVG into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {svg | dataBase64 (SVG or SVGZ bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the SVG's objects (and the images, patterns and symbols they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.pasteInPlace

vectorcraft.label: Swatch Conflicts
vectorcraft.params: {} → {swatches: [{name, document, clipboard, spot}]} the global or spot swatches the copied objects use whose name the active document gives another colour (`document`/`clipboard`: #rrggbb): Paste asks Merge or Add for each (pass the answer as edit.paste* {swatchConflict}). Pasting back into the document the objects came from raises none

vectorcraft.label: Clipboard as PNG
vectorcraft.params: {scale?: 1 (pixels per point, up to 64)} → {dataBase64, width, height (px), warnings} the copied objects cropped to their visual bounds, transparent around them (dataBase64 null when the clipboard is empty); warnings as for document.export (an image that couldn't be decoded, type in the fallback font or that doesn't fit its frame)

vectorcraft.label: Clipboard as PDF
vectorcraft.params: {} → {dataBase64, warnings} a one-page PDF of the copied objects, the page their visual bounds (dataBase64 null when the clipboard is empty); warnings as for document.export

vectorcraft.label: Clipboard as Text
vectorcraft.params: {} → {text} the copied type objects' text, one object per line (null unless every copied object is type, or a group of type)

vectorcraft.label: Clipboard Formats
vectorcraft.params: {} → {flavours: [mime…]} what Copy offers other apps for the current clipboard, best first, by the Clipboard Handling preferences: text/plain (a type-only copy's text, else the SVG markup with copyAsSvg when the images it embeds total at most 1 MiB), image/svg+xml (copyAsSvg), application/pdf (copyAsPdf), image/png (always; PDF and PNG only for objects with an area); the app publishes them on Copy and Cut

vectorcraft.label: Load Image into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {dataBase64 (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes), mime?: the type the system clipboard gave (an image/… type; the format is read from the bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the image, embedded at 100% of its physical size (its resolution, else 72 ppi), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, width, height (pt), pixelWidth, pixelHeight}; then run edit.paste

vectorcraft.label: Load Text into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {text, center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with point text of `text` (one paragraph per line; trailing line breaks dropped) in the default type style, centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.paste

vectorcraft.label: Load PDF into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {dataBase64, page?: 1, password? (an encrypted PDF), editingData?: false (true: the data is a .ai or .ait file, read as document.open reads it; when document.open would use its editing data, every object of that data comes in, each layer's objects in stacking order and a hidden layer's objects hidden; else page `page`), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the objects of one PDF page, or of a .ai file's editing data (with the images, patterns and swatches they use; a .ai saved without PDF compatibility: every object of its editing data, as document.open reads it, with or without editingData), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; then run edit.paste

vectorcraft.label: Load Metafile into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {dataBase64 (EMF or WMF bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the picture's objects (paths, clipping groups, images, point type; the images they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning; then run edit.paste

vectorcraft.label: Load EPS into Clipboard
vectorcraft.params: {dataBase64 (EPS or other PostScript bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the picture's objects as document.open reads an EPS (editable paths, type and images, with the images, patterns and swatches they use; a hidden layer's objects hidden), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; then run edit.paste

vectorcraft.label: Artwork Colors
vectorcraft.params: {} → {colors: [{key: colour identity ("rgb 255 0 0", "cmyk 0 100 100 0", "gray 40", "lab 55 60 -40"), hex, count, swatch?: the global swatch it is linked to}]} unique colours used by the selection (fills, strokes, gradient stops, text, mesh points and the tiles of pattern fills and strokes), most used first

vectorcraft.label: Recolor Artwork
vectorcraft.params: {map: rows [{from: [colour keys (recolor.colors) or "#rrggbb" (every colour shown as that hex)], to: colour (hex, key, {c,m,y,k} or {l,a,b}) | null, exclude?: false (the row's colours are kept)}] | {"key or #rrggbb": colour, …} (one row per colour), method?: "exact" (default)|"preserveTints"|"scaleTints"|"tintsShades"|"hueShift" (how a row's colours take its new colour, relative to the row's darkest, average or most saturated colour), limitTo?: swatch library id or name; or "document" (the document's swatches): new colours snap to its nearest colour, group?: colour group to rewrite, groupColors?: [colour] (what `group` is rewritten with; default: the rows' new colours, in order, excluded rows left out), rename?: the group's new name, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true} recolour the selection (gradients, text, meshes, image pixels and pattern tiles included; each new colour keeps the model of the one it replaces (model?: "keep" default | "new" (the new colour's own model, so a CMYK colour replacing RGB art gives CMYK art) | "document" (the document's colour mode)), except a library swatch's with limitTo: art takes the swatch itself, linked to a global or spot colour at its tints, and the swatch joins the document's swatches) and the group, as one undo step → {changed, swatches: [names added to the document's swatches], note?: set when a colour kept a model other than its new colour's (see model)}

vectorcraft.label: Reduce Colors
vectorcraft.params: {colors?: n (rows; default: one per colour, with the tints of a global swatch in its row), method?: as recolor.apply; default scaleTints (picks each row's colour), preserve?: {white?: true, black?: true, grays?: false} (left out of the rows), limitTo?: as recolor.apply (new colours snap to it)} group the selection's colours into rows of similar colours (k-means in Lab, weighted by use) → {map: [{from: [keys, the row's colour first], to: key}], preserved: [keys], method}

vectorcraft.label: Randomize Colors
vectorcraft.params: {map: rows as recolor.apply, order?: true (shuffle the new colours among the rows that aren't excluded), saturationBrightness?: false (random saturation and brightness, hue kept), seed?: 0} → {map: the rows with their new colours as keys}

vectorcraft.label: Open Document
vectorcraft.params: {path | name | dataBase64 (a file's path, or its name with its bytes), pages?: "2-3, 5" (PDF/.ai: 1-based, default all; one artboard each) | page?: n, cropTo?: bounding|art|crop (default)|trim|bleed|media (the box each artboard gets; bounding: the art's bounds; trim: the bleed box round it becomes the document's bleed; a PDF-compatible .ai or a PDF saved with its editing data opens on its trim boxes for crop), password? (encrypted PDFs; see document.pdfInfo), textAs?: text (default: point type per line, lines wrapped in a frame as area type where they lay out the same, in the file's fonts by name; missing ones are listed in warnings) | outlines (glyph paths), layers?: true (default: optional content groups become layers with their visibility, print state and lock — art that is off comes in as a hidden layer; other art goes to a layer per page) | false (one layer per page, without the art that is off; Save then asks for a name), editingData?: true (default: an EPS, .ai or PDF that carries its editor's own copy of the art opens from it, with its layers, hidden objects, guides, artboards and the art outside them; a .ai or PDF whose type shows opens from its PDF part with textAs: outlines) | "always" (as true, and a .ai's editing copy is used even where it draws differently from its PDF part, which can be older; the warnings say so) | false (only what its page or PDF part prints, for print pipelines; a .ai saved without PDF compatibility then can't be opened), colorMode?: rgb|cmyk (the mode the document opens in, its colours converted as file.documentColorMode does, grays? as there; default: the file's — a PDF keeps CMYK, Gray and spot inks (spot swatches at a tint) and opens in CMYK when painted mostly in CMYK), grays?: as file.documentColorMode, dxf?: {layout?: "Model" (default) | a paper layout's name (document.dxfInfo lists them), unit?, scale? (the ratio: 1 unit of the art = scale drawing units; default: the drawing at 1:1 in its own unit), fit?: false (scale to fit an artboard of fitTo?: [612, 792], turned to the art's orientation), scaleLineweights?: false (lineweights scale with the art), center?: true (false: the drawing's origin on the artboard's bottom-left corner; fitted art's bottom-left corner), mergeLayers?: false (all art on one layer)} (DXF), crop?: as cropTo (its older name)} → {index, title, format, warnings, restored, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks: [{name, path, ids}]}; any readable format (see document.formats): .vectorcraft/.drawcraft, .svg/.svgz, .pdf/.ai, .ait, ASCII .dxf (each DXF layer with art a layer; blocks symbols; what can't come in is listed in warnings), PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/TIFF/BMP (an image opens as a document of its size at the resolution it declares, as file.place sizes it; 72 ppi, 1 px = 1 pt, when it declares none), .emf/.wmf (one artboard, the picture's frame; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning), .eps and PostScript .ai (one artboard, the bounding box: an EPS file VectorCraft wrote restores the document it carries, restored: true; other files are read by a PostScript interpreter — paths, colours and spot inks, clips, gradients, images, type in the fonts named — and come in as their TIFF preview, with a warning, when their PostScript can't be read). A PDF/.ai/.ait or SVG saved with Preserve Editing restores the native document it carries (restored: true; a PDF only when no pages are picked), unless the file was changed elsewhere since or the data can't be read: then its artwork is imported and the first warning says why. Templates (native templates, .ait) open as a new untitled document; a restored .ai keeps its path (Save writes .ai again). Linked images are read from their files (looked for at their path, then relative to the document): missing ones show their saved preview (links.relink), modified ones are read again only with Preferences › Update Links: Automatically (else links.update). An SVG's <image> files (relative links from the SVG's folder) stay linked, SVG files become art, missing ones a placeholder in their box (a warning and missingLinks)

vectorcraft.label: List Folder
vectorcraft.params: {path} the files and folders in folder `path`, by name: what an agent may open there (held to the automation read root when one is in force) → {path, entries: [{name, kind: file|folder|link, size? (files, bytes)}], truncated (more than 5000 entries)} (#1163)

vectorcraft.label: Serialize Document
vectorcraft.params: {format?: vectorcraft (default)|template|svg|svgz|pdf|ai|png|jpg|webp|gif|png8|txt|dxf|eps|emf|wmf|tiff|bmp|tga|psd (ait, a .ait template, is written by file.saveAsTemplate), …the format's options (see document.formats; SVG ones also as svg: {…}), selectedOnly?: false (the selected objects alone, in their layers)} → {text, warnings} for svg (plus dataBase64, the file, when its encoding isn't UTF-8), else {dataBase64, warnings}; an SVG of several artboards also gives files: [{name, text}], linked images linked: [{name, dataBase64}]

vectorcraft.label: Export Document
vectorcraft.params: {path?, format?: svg|svgz|pdf|ai|png|jpg|webp|gif|png8|txt|dxf|eps|emf|wmf|tiff|bmp|tga|psd|vectorcraft|template (default: from the path's extension, else png; png8 writes an indexed .png; ait, a .ait template, is written by file.saveAsTemplate; an exporter plug-in's format is plugin.<plug-in id>, which an extension only it lists picks too), params?: {…} (an exporter plug-in's parameters; missing ones take their defaults, see plugin.info), selectedOnly?: false (the selected objects alone, in their layers), artboard?: 0, artboards?: [i…], rect?: [x, y, width, height] (raster formats: that area of the page in points, y down, instead of an artboard; not with artboard, artboards, range or useArtboards), range?: "1-3, 5" | "all" (1-based; PDF and .ai write one page per artboard, default all; SVG writes one file per artboard, {stem}-{artboard}.svg; raster formats write one artboard), useArtboards?: true (raster: one file per chosen artboard, default all, {stem}-{artboard}.{ext}; pdf/ai: every page) | false (pdf/ai/raster: the bounds of the visible art; SVG has it as an SVG option), ppi?: 72 (raster formats: pixels per inch, stored in the file; wins over scale), scale?: 1 (pixels per point), background?: transparent|white|black|"#rrggbb" (jpg: white when transparent), antiAlias?: none|art (default)|type (text snapped to pixels), interlaced?: false (png, Adam7), embedIcc?: true (png: an sRGB chunk marks the colours as sRGB), quality?: 90 (jpg: 0–100), colorModel?: rgb|cmyk|gray (jpg), method?: baseline|optimized|progressive, scans?: 3 (3–5, progressive), embedIcc?: true, imageMap?: none|client|server (an HTML or NCSA map of the objects with a URL, written as <stem>.html / <stem>.map), colors?: 256 (gif/png8: 2–256), reduction?: perceptual|selective (default)|adaptive|web|blackWhite|gray, dither?: none|diffusion (default)|pattern|noise, ditherAmount?: 100, transparency?: true, matte?: white|"#rrggbb"|none, interlaced?, lossless?: true (webp: lossy WebP isn't available yet: written lossless, with a warning), encoding?: utf8|utf16 (txt: the stories in stacking order, back to front, a thread once; utf16 with a byte order mark), lineEndings?: lf|crlf, selectionOnly?: false, svg?: {styling, outlineText, images, objectIds, decimals, minify, responsive, useArtboards, preserveEditing, metadata, fewerTspans, hiddenLayers, encoding, profile, embedFonts} (see document.formats), …the SVG options given flat instead, …the PDF options of document.exportPdf, …the DXF options of document.exportDxf (useArtboards: one drawing per artboard), …the EPS options of document.exportEps (useArtboards: one file per artboard, {stem}_{artboard}.eps; else the visible art), …emf and wmf write one picture of the artboard (useArtboards: true one file per chosen artboard, false the bounds of the visible art; EMF keeps curves, clipping, transparent images and gradients as images clipped to their shape; WMF flattens curves into polygons behind a placeable header; what a format leaves out comes back in warnings), colorModel?: rgb|cmyk|gray (tiff: rgb keeps transparency as an alpha channel), lzw?: true, byteOrder?: little|big, embedIcc?: true, colorModel?: rgb|gray (bmp), depth?: 24 (bmp: 1 black and white, 4|8 a palette by reduction and dither, 16, 24, 32 with alpha), fileFormat?: windows|os2 (1, 4, 8 or 24 bits), rle?: false (4 and 8 bits, windows), flipRows?: false (top-down rows), depth?: 24 (tga: 16 one-bit alpha, 24, 32 with alpha), colorModel?: rgb|cmyk|gray (psd), layers?: true (each top-level layer a pixel layer with its opacity and blend mode; a background colour is a Background layer; false: one flat image, on white), maxEditability?: false (layers and sublayers become groups, each object a layer named as in the Layers panel, text by its text; clipping, masked or knockout layers stay one layer), hiddenLayers?: false (hidden layers and objects written hidden instead of left out), embedIcc?: true (at most 30000 pixels a side; formats without alpha are flattened on white)} → {path, format, bytes, warnings, files?: [path…] (several), linked?: [path…] (linked images, image maps)}; no path → {dataBase64, format, bytes, warnings, files?: [{name, dataBase64}], linked?: [{name, dataBase64}]}. Never changes the document's path

vectorcraft.label: Export Selection…
vectorcraft.params: {path?, format?: png|jpg|webp|svg|svgz|pdf|ai|gif|png8|tiff|bmp|tga|psd|txt|dxf|eps|emf|wmf|vectorcraft|template (default: from the extension, else png), scale?: 1, …the format's options} the selected objects cropped to their bounds (template layers left out) → {path, format, bytes, warnings, bounds} (no path → {dataBase64, format, bytes, warnings, bounds}); warnings say what the format approximated or left out, as for document.export

vectorcraft.label: Export for Screens
vectorcraft.params: {folder?, zip?: false (one store-only .zip of every file: no folder → {name, dataBase64, bytes, files: [name…]}; with a folder it is written there → {path, bytes, files}), artboards?: [index…] | range?: "1-3" (default all), assets?: [asset id…] (instead of artboards: each asset's art alone, cropped to its bounds and named after the asset; see assets.list), layers?: [layer id…] (instead of artboards: each layer's art alone, sublayers included, named after the layer), selection?: one|each (instead of artboards: the selected art as one file, or a file per selected object, named after it), fullDocument?: false (one file per format instead: a PDF of every artboard, other formats the bounds of all visible art, named after the document), includeBleed?: false (artboards grown by the document's bleed), exportPreset?: (a preset of document.exportPresets.list: its settings, under these params), subfolders?: false (each row's files in a sub-folder: its folder, else its size for raster (1x, 2x, 100w…) or its format (SVG, PDF)), folders?: none|rows (as subfolders)|format (a folder per extension: png, svg, pdf…)|item (a folder per artboard, asset, layer or object)|itemFormat (item/extension) (default: rows with subfolders or a preset, else none), name?: (a file name pattern instead of the item's name, with <filename> for the document, <name> for the artboard, asset, layer or object, <index> from 1, #### for the counter zero-padded to the run of #, <format>, <scale>, <suffix> (else the row's suffix ends the name), YYYYMMDD, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY, <date>, <time>, <YYYY>, <MM>, <DD>, <hh>, <mm> and <ss>; a trailing .ext is dropped, as in `COMPANY-Logo-<filename>-####-YYYYMMDD`; different files it names alike get -2, -3…), counterStart?: 1, counterPer?: item (every file of an item has its number)|file, date?: YYYY-MM-DD (the date the pattern uses; default today, UTC), preset?: mobile (PNG 1x, 2x, 3x) | density (PNG 0.75x–4x in ldpi…xxxhdpi sub-folders) instead of formats (turns subfolders on), formats?: [{format: png|png8|jpg|webp|gif|tiff|bmp|tga|psd|svg|svgz|pdf|eps|ai|vectorcraft, scale?: 1 | "2x" | "100w" | "100h" | "72ppi", width?: px | height?: px | ppi? (raster only; width, then height, then ppi win over scale), suffix?: (raster default: @2x, @100w, @100h, none at 1x; vector formats drop size suffixes), folder?: (its sub-folder), quality?: (jpg 0–100), …the format's options (antiAlias, background, preset (pdf)…)}], settings?: {png|png8|jpg|webp|gif|tiff|bmp|tga|psd|svg|svgz|pdf|eps|ai|vectorcraft: {…options for every row of that format}} (rows' own options win), prefix?, antiAlias?: none|art|type (raster rows without their own), openLocation?: (remembered; the app shows the files after exporting)} one file per artboard and format (a PDF holds its artboard alone; artboards with the same name, in any case, get -2, -3…; an unnamed one is Artboard-N) → {files: [path…]}; no folder → {files: [{name, dataBase64}]} (names include sub-folders: 2x/Icon@2x.png); every reply has warnings: [the encoders' warnings for the files, each once: an image that couldn't be decoded, type written in the fallback font…]. eps, ai and vectorcraft rows write a document of the item alone (its one artboard). The params (but zip and assets) are remembered in the document (document.exportSettings; not an undo step)

vectorcraft.label: Export Presets
vectorcraft.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, settings}]} the built-in batch export presets (Logo Package, Print-Ready PDF), then the saved ones; any name works as document.exportForScreens' exportPreset

vectorcraft.label: Save Export Preset
vectorcraft.params: {name, settings: {formats, settings, preset, name, prefix, counterStart, counterPer, folders, subfolders, includeBleed, antiAlias, folder, fullDocument} (as document.exportForScreens; other keys are left out)} save (or replace) a batch export preset, kept with the preferences; built-in names are refused → {name, created, settings}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Export Preset
vectorcraft.params: {name} delete a saved batch export preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted}

vectorcraft.label: Batch
vectorcraft.params: {label?, commands: [{command, params}], artboard?: index (the active artboard; the app passes it: each edit.pasteInPlace, edit.pasteInFront, edit.pasteInBack, object.align, object.distribute, object.distributeSpacing or select.allOnArtboard step that names none gets it, and each artboard.fitToArt or artboard.fitToSelection step that names no index gets it as index, or the last artboard of a document with fewer)} run several commands as ONE undo step (one in each document they edit: steps may open, switch, close or revert documents); stops at the first error and rolls everything back, documents included

vectorcraft.label: Batch…
vectorcraft.params: {commands: [{command, params}] (the action's steps), source?: folder (default) | datasets, folder? (required for folder: the source folder), includeSubdirs?: false, destination?: none (default: leave each file open) | saveAndClose (save over the source and close) | folder (save or export into destinationFolder and close), destinationFolder? (required when destination is folder; also the folder Override Save/Export write into), overrideOpen?: true (skip document.open / file.open steps: the batch opens each source file), overrideSave?: true (point document.save / file.save / file.saveAs at destinationFolder/{stem}.{ext}), overrideExport?: true (point document.export / document.exportForScreens / document.exportSelection the same way), stopOnError?: true, label?} play the commands on every readable file in folder (and its subfolders when includeSubdirs), or on every data set of the open document (source: datasets; File + Data Set Name for the folder destination and Override Save/Export, with `/`, `\`, `:`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `|`, `?`, `*` and control characters in the data set's name as `-`, and `-2`, `-3`… added to a name already used). Caps: 500 files or data sets, 8 folder levels, 256 steps. Batches cannot nest. → {processed: [{path|dataset, result|error}…], count, failed, stopped}

vectorcraft.label: File Formats
vectorcraft.params: {} → {formats: [{id, label, extensions, mime, read, write, raster, options: {name: {type, default, description}}, plugin?: the id of the exporter plug-in that adds the format (its id is plugin.<plug-in id>; see plugin.list)}], readable: [id…], writable: [id…], openExtensions: [ext…], unsupported: [{id, label, extensions, hint}] (formats asked for that can be neither opened nor written, such as DWG and PICT, with what to use instead)}

vectorcraft.label: PDF Info
vectorcraft.params: {path | name? | dataBase64 (a file's path, or its bytes), password?, thumbnail?: page (1-based), thumbnailSize?: 160 (px, longest side), cropTo?: crop (the thumbnail's box)} → {pages, needsPassword, wrongPassword?, pageInfo: [{width, height (pt, as shown), rotation, boxes: {media, crop, bleed, trim, art: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (PDF space, pt)}}], thumbnail?: PNG dataBase64}; a page whose UserUnit (PDF 1.6) is above 1 gives its size and boxes in pt, its numbers times the UserUnit (one above 75,000 counts as 75,000); an encrypted PDF without its password → {pages: 0, needsPassword: true}; a PostScript file (an EPS, a .ps file, a .ai in PostScript form) → {pages: 1, needsPassword: false, pageInfo: [{width, height (its bounding box, a US Letter page without one), rotation: 0, boxes: {}}]} (password and cropTo don't apply; thumbnail: 1 shows what the page prints)

vectorcraft.label: Export for Screens Settings

vectorcraft.label: Save Document
vectorcraft.params: {path?, format?: vectorcraft|template|pdf|svg|svgz|ai (default: the path's extension, else the document's own format), options?: {…the format's options, see file.formatOptions; default: as last saved}, svg?: {…SVG options} (an SVG save keeps hidden layers, display:none, unless hiddenLayers is false), …the SVG and PDF options given flat instead, compress?: bool (native, also in options: gzip; default: the useCompression preference), version?: 4 (3, 2 or 1: for older VectorCraft versions; 1 and 2 are never compressed), preview?: false (embed a PNG of the first artboard, at most 256 px), separateArtboards?: false (native and .ai: also save each artboard of `range` to <name>-<artboard>.<ext> beside the file, holding that artboard and the art touching it; the result's files lists every file written), range?: "1-3, 5"|"all" (default; with separateArtboards), includeLinked?: false (keep linked files' own pixels, not just their previews; they stay linked), embedProfiles?: true (carry the ICC profiles loaded from files that the document is tagged with; opening the file installs them where missing), pdfCompatible?: false for native (also carry a PDF of every artboard) | true for .ai (false: blank pages, only the native document; a .ai file's compress, default true, is its compression.compressText), modified?: Unix seconds|null (the File Info modified date, and created date when there is none, a save to a file stamps; default now, recorded in the journal so a replay matches; null: leave the dates)} → {path, format, bytes, warnings, files?: [path…] (the file and its artboards' files), linked?: [path…] (images an SVG links to)}. Save writes one artboard, except a .ai file: a PDF-compatible file of every artboard carrying the native document (preserveEditing always on; PDF options flat or in options), which document.open restores exactly; separateArtboards writes more files, one per artboard. Without a path it writes the document's own file in its own format: a document opened from or saved as SVG/PDF saves as that again (warnings name what the format loses). No path known (never saved, converted from an older version, restored by Data Recovery, or another format) → {dataBase64, format, name, folder?, warnings} and the document stays modified

vectorcraft.label: Save As…
vectorcraft.params: {…as document.save} {path?, format?: vectorcraft|template|pdf|svg|svgz|ai (default: the path's extension, else the document's own; ait, a .ait template, is written by file.saveAsTemplate), options?, svg?, modified?} the document takes on the new path, name and format (except a template, which is always a copy) → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name, folder?, warnings}

vectorcraft.label: Save a Copy…
vectorcraft.params: {…as document.save} {path?, format?, options?} write a copy; the document keeps its path, title and modified state → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name: "<name> copy.<ext>", folder?, warnings}

vectorcraft.label: Save as Template…
vectorcraft.params: {…as document.save} {path? (saved with the format's extension: one naming another format is replaced, and one is added to a name without it), format?: template (default) | ait (also when format is not given and the path ends in .ait), compress?, version?, preview?} a template that opens as a new untitled document: a native template (.vctemplate), or a PDF-compatible .ait written as a .ai file is (the .ai options and the PDF options, as document.save takes them for .ai; aiVersion 7 is an error); the document is unchanged → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name: "<name> template.<ext>", folder: the Templates folder (preference templatesFolder), warnings}

vectorcraft.label: New from Template…
vectorcraft.params: {path} or {name, dataBase64}: open a template (or any readable file) as a new untitled document → {index, title, format, warnings}

vectorcraft.label: Revert
vectorcraft.params: {confirmed?: bool (the app's own: it asks first, then runs the command with it)} discard the changes: reload the saved file into the same tab (history cleared; the tab keeps its place and view). Saved, modified documents only; if the file can't be read the document is left as it is → {path}. The app asks first (a confirm dialog) unless confirmed: true

vectorcraft.label: Transform
vectorcraft.params: {matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f], copy?: bool, ids?, strokes?: bool, corners?: bool, typeAreas?: bool, anchors?: bool, objects?: bool (Transform Objects, default true; false: the art stays and, with patterns, only its pattern tiles transform), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} apply an affine to the selection (or ids); anchors (without ids or copy): paths with anchors selected with Direct Selection have only those anchors and their handles transformed, as the Transform tools and object.move/rotate/scale/reflect/shear do (default: the whole objects); strokes/corners: Scale Strokes & Effects / Scale Corners (default: the preferences); typeAreas: area type among them (not type inside a group) reshapes its frame by the matrix and its text reflows at its size, as a bounding-box handle drag does (default: the type transforms too)

vectorcraft.label: Move…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), dx, dy, copy?, objects?: bool (Transform Objects, default true; false: the art stays and, with patterns, only its pattern tiles transform), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), typeAreas?: bool (area type: the frame is reshaped and the text reflows at its size)}. With anchors selected with Direct Selection (and no copy), only those anchors and their handles transform, about the centre of their own box.

vectorcraft.label: Rotate…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection), angle: deg (counter-clockwise), absolute?: bool (angle is the bounding box's new angle, not an amount), origin?: [x,y] (default: the bounding box centre), copy?, objects?: bool (Transform Objects, default true; false: the art stays and, with patterns, only its pattern tiles transform), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles), typeAreas?: bool (area type: the frame is reshaped and the text reflows at its size)} → {ids}. With anchors selected with Direct Selection (and no copy), only those anchors and their handles transform, about the centre of their own box.

With anchors selected with Direct Selection (and no copy), only those anchors and their handles transform, about the centre of their own box.

With anchors selected with Direct Selection (and no copy), only those anchors and their handles transform, about the centre of their own box.

vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the topmost selected object (a path, compound path or text, which loses its paint) clips the others: compound holes, even-odd fills and glyph outlines clip as drawn. Paint given to the clipping path later (paint commands with its id) shows: its fill behind the clipped art, its stroke over it → {id} of the clip group

vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} the selected clip groups become plain groups; their clipping path (path, compound path or text) stays, with the paint it has (none unless painted after Make)

vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, name?, visible?, locked? (visible: false or locked: true deselects every selected object hidden or locked after the call, the key object included), opacity?: 0..100, blend?: "Multiply"…, isolate?, knockout?: "on"|"off"|"neutral"|bool (true = on, false = neutral), knockoutShape?: bool, data?: {key: "value" | null (removes it)} (the object's own data, SVG data-* attributes: {pivot: "100,180"} is data-pivot; document.node → attrs.data)}

vectorcraft.label: Align
vectorcraft.params: {horizontal?: "left"|"center"|"right", vertical?: "top"|"center"|"bottom", to?: "selection"|"artboard"|"key" (default: the key object when the selection has one, select.key, else the selection; a key guide, select.key {guide}, stays put and the objects line up on its line: a vertical guide sets where left, center and right go and vertical alignment leaves them, a horizontal one the other way round; aligning to the key, the other selected ruler guides move too: a vertical guide to the key's left edge, center or right edge, a horizontal one to its top, center or bottom; aligning to the artboard moves selected guides to its edges too (#3463), and with only guides selected aligning to the selection moves them to their collective bounds), artboard?: index (0-based; with to: "artboard", the artboard to align to; the app passes the active one; default: the artboard under the center of the selection, else the first), bounds?: "preview"|"geometric" (default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} With anchor points selected (Direct Selection), the points align instead: to their own bounds, or to the artboard (#1180)

vectorcraft.label: Distribute
vectorcraft.params: {horizontal?: "left"|"center"|"right", vertical?: "top"|"center"|"bottom", spacing?: pt (used with a key, select.key: the key object, or the key guide, select.key {guide}, stays put and the lines are placed this far apart, outward from its line, in their order on that line; 0 puts them all on its line; a key guide along the axis leaves everything where it is; not used without a key or with anchor points selected), to?: "selection"|"artboard"|"key" (default: the key while there is one, else the selection; "key" without spacing distributes as "selection" does; not used with anchor points selected, or with spacing and a key object; with a key guide, "selection" or "artboard" distributes without it as the key), artboard?: index (0-based; with to: "artboard", the artboard to distribute across; the app passes the active one; default: as object.align's), bounds?: "preview"|"geometric" (default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} space the selected objects' left edges, centers or right edges (top edges, centers or bottom edges) in their order on that line, with the selected ruler guides across the axis (vertical ones for horizontal; #1597): a guide has no size, so its edges and center are its line, and guides along the axis stay. Without spacing and a key they are spaced evenly, the first and last stay put, and fewer than three don't move; with spacing and a key, see spacing (two are enough); with to: "artboard", the first one's left (top) edge goes to the artboard's left (top) edge, the last one's right (bottom) edge goes to the artboard's right (bottom) edge, and two are enough. With anchor points selected (Direct Selection), the points are spaced evenly between the first and the last along the axis instead (#1636)

vectorcraft.label: Distribute Spacing
vectorcraft.params: {axis: "horizontal"|"vertical", spacing?: pt (the key object, select.key, or the key guide, select.key {guide}, stays put and the others are spaced from it; a key guide along the axis leaves everything where it is), to?: "selection"|"artboard"|"key" (used without spacing and without anchor points selected, and with a key guide; default: the key while there is one, else the selection; "key" without spacing spaces as "selection" does), artboard?: index (0-based; with to: "artboard", the artboard to space across; the app passes the active one; default: as object.align's), bounds?: "preview"|"geometric" (default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes), patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} without spacing, make the gaps between the selected objects equal, in the order of their left (top) edges, with the selected ruler guides across the axis as items with no size (#1597; guides along the axis stay): the first item's left (top) edge and the last one's right (bottom) edge stay put, or with to: "artboard" go to the artboard's left (top) and right (bottom) edges. With anchor points selected (Direct Selection), the points are spaced evenly along the axis instead, or `spacing` apart from the first (#1636)

vectorcraft.label: Set Bounds
vectorcraft.params: {x?, y?, width?, height?, reference?: 0..8 (9-point grid; a number past 8 is read as 8), proportional?, strokes?, corners?, copy?: bool, patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns), typeAreas?: bool (area type: the frame is reshaped and the text reflows at its size), objects?: bool (Transform Objects, as object.move)} (Transform panel; width/height and the reference point follow the bounding box, rotated with rotated objects; x, y are page coordinates; with Use Preview Bounds the values measure the visual bounds; strokes/corners as object.scale; with anchor points selected (Direct Selection) and no copy, the values are the box around those points, square to the page, and only they move or scale, as with object.move (#1824))

vectorcraft.label: Live Shape Properties
vectorcraft.params: {id?, ids?, radius?: pt (or % of each corner's maximum when `relativeRadii` is true), kind?: "round"|"invertedRound"|"chamfer", relativeRadii?: bool (Relative rounding, as in the reference app: store radii as fractions of each corner's maximum so they scale with the shape), corners?: [i…], items?: [{id, corners?: [i…]}] (several objects, each with its own corners, in place of ids and corners: the canvas's corner widgets across a selection), sides?: n, polygonAngle?: degrees (counterclockwise from its first vertex straight up), polygonRadius?: pt (centre to vertex), sideLength?: pt (sets the radius), makeSidesEqual?: true (a polygon scaled unevenly: drops the uneven scale and shear, keeping its centre, angle and mean radius), pieStart?, pieEnd?: degrees (an ellipse's pie, counterclockwise from 3 o'clock; 0 to 360 is the whole ellipse), invertPie?: true (swaps them: the other part of the ellipse)} (Live Corners on any path: radius and kind set its corners (anchors that aren't smooth, where two sides, straight or curved (#1144), meet at an angle): `corners` (anchor indices of the path with its corners uncut, counting every subpath's anchors in order: a rectangle's 0 top-left, 1 top-right, 2 bottom-right, 3 bottom-left; a polygon's from the first vertex clockwise), else the corners with a Direct-Selected anchor, else every corner; each radius is drawn no larger than half the corner's shorter side allows; a path that isn't a live shape keeps its uncut outline so its corners stay editable, and is plain again once none is cut; sides: a polygon's, which keep the radius they shared; the polygon params apply in that order: sides, makeSidesEqual, polygonAngle, then sideLength or else polygonRadius)
