vectorcraft.params: {value?} make the page a knockout group (default: toggle): its layers (the contents of neutral layers) hide what they cover instead of showing it through their transparency; saved with the document and written to PDF → {value}

vectorcraft.label: New Layer…
vectorcraft.params: {name?, top?: bool, color?, template?, locked?, visible?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?} a layer directly above the current layer, at its level (a sublayer beside a current sublayer); `top`: above all layers (Ctrl-click the button). Options as layer.setProps → {id}

vectorcraft.label: New Sublayer…
vectorcraft.params: {parent?: layer id (default: the highlighted row's layer, else the current layer), name?, …options as layer.new} a sublayer on top of the parent's contents → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Selection
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} delete rows: layers, sublayers, groups or objects with what they hold (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer). The last layer stays → {deleted}

vectorcraft.label: Duplicate Selection
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} copy rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), each just above its original; a layer's copy is named `<name> copy`. The copies are highlighted → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Set Current Layer
vectorcraft.params: {id} click a row: it alone is highlighted, and the layer it is (or the layer it is in) becomes the current layer, where new art goes. Not an undo step → {id, layer}

vectorcraft.label: Highlight Rows
vectorcraft.params: {ids, mode?: "set"|"add"|"toggle"} highlight Layers panel rows (Shift-click: a range, Ctrl-click: toggle one); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step → {rows}

vectorcraft.label: Layer Options…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id? (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), name? (with prefs.identifyObjectsBy xmlId: a valid XML ID, stored as the object name), visible?, locked?, template?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?: 0..100|false, color?: index 0..26|"#rrggbb"|preset name} Layer Options; rows that are not layers take name, visible and locked. Template on also locks the layer and dims its images to 50% (unless given); off unlocks it and stops dimming. One undo step

vectorcraft.label: Collect in New Layer
vectorcraft.params: {ids?} move rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was (a sublayer when they are in a layer), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too) → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Select Art
vectorcraft.params: {id, add?: bool} the Layers panel's selection column: select the visible, unlocked art of a layer (its sublayers' too), or the object itself; `add` (Shift-click) adds it to the selection, or removes it when it is all selected already → {selected: [..]}

vectorcraft.label: Move Rows
vectorcraft.params: {ids|id, target, place?: "above"|"below"|"inside" (default inside), copy?: bool} drag rows in the Layers panel: above or below the target row (beside it, in its layer or group), or inside a layer or group (on top of its contents). Layers go only in layers or at the top level, objects in layers and groups; an object placed beside a top-level layer goes inside it. A row never goes into itself; a locked layer or group takes nothing. `copy` (Alt-drag) moves copies. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one moved into a hidden layer or group, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Reorder
vectorcraft.params: {id, parent?: id (null = top level), index} put a row at `index` (0 = bottom) of `parent` (layers only at the top level or in layers), deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too)

vectorcraft.label: New Artboard
vectorcraft.params: {x?, y?, width?, height?, name?, color?: color (its background color, as artboard.setProps takes it; default: none)} (default place: right of the last)

vectorcraft.label: Delete Artboard
vectorcraft.params: {index | indices: [index…]} delete artboards (with their guides) in one step; one is always left, and a locked one is an error

vectorcraft.label: Artboard Options…
vectorcraft.params: {index | artboards: [{index, name?, color?, locked?, x?, y?, width?, height?}…] (several artboards in one undo step, each with its own fields; the art inside each before any of them changes goes with it, and an object inside several goes with the first listed that moves or scales its art), name?, color?: color ("#rrggbb", {c,m,y,k}, … as the paint commands take: the background color the canvas draws the artboard's paper in, multiplied with the Simulate Colored Paper color while that is on; exports and print leave it out) | null (no background color), locked?: bool (the Artboards panel's lock column: a locked artboard keeps its rectangle (a new x, y, width or height is an error unless locked is false), can't be moved, deleted or cut, and Rearrange and Fit to Artwork Bounds leave it as it is; the art on it (each object of a layer or sublayer whose bounds with strokes overlap it, a group as one object) acts as locked art until it is unlocked: clicks, marquees, select.set, select.all and the tools pass over it (art drawn or pasted onto it stays selected and editable until a selection leaves it out or it is moved off the locked artboards), it is deselected, and when another artboard moves or scales it stays unless lockedAndHidden), x?, y?, width?, height?, moveArt?: bool (default false; a position-only change moves the contained art with its artboard), scaleArt?: bool (Scale Artwork with Artboard: resized, the artboard takes the art fully inside it (locked and hidden art only with lockedAndHidden?: bool, default prefs moveLockedWithArtboard) and its guides from its old rectangle onto the new one, each side by its own ratio; strokes/corners/patterns as object.scale), strokes?: bool, corners?: bool, patterns?: bool (the three as object.scale, for art that moves or scales with the artboard), lockedAndHidden?: bool (locked and hidden art moves along; default: the preference; recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} → null, or with scaleArt {scaled: the art scaled}

vectorcraft.label: Fit to Artwork Bounds
vectorcraft.params: {index?: n | indices?: [n…] (0-based; the app passes the selected artboards: the Artboard tool's, else the active one; default: the first)} each artboard fits the art on it that shows (with its strokes and effects; hidden objects and layers, guides and template layers don't count), in one undo step: an object counts for every artboard its bounds overlap, and a group or clipping layer counts as one object; an artboard with no art, or a locked one, stays as it is, and the command fails when every artboard it names is locked or none has art

vectorcraft.label: Fit to Selected Art
vectorcraft.params: {index?: n (0-based; the app passes the active artboard; default: the first)} the artboard fits the selected art (with its strokes); a locked artboard stays as it is (an error when the fit would change it)

vectorcraft.label: Make/Release Clipping Mask
vectorcraft.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the one highlighted layer or group row, else the one selected group, else the current layer)} make: its top object (a path, compound path or text, which loses its paint) clips the rest and moves to the bottom (new art added on top is clipped); release: it stops clipping, the clipping path stays unpainted → {clip}

vectorcraft.label: Target
vectorcraft.params: {id, add?: bool (Shift-click: the item joins the selection, or leaves it when all selected; nothing is targeted)} target a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle in the Layers panel does: a layer gets its visible, unlocked art (its sublayers' too) selected and becomes the current layer, and appearance.*, effect.*, transparency.* and the opacity-mask commands without `ids` then act on the layer itself; anything else is selected. Any other selection change ends the targeting (`document.inspect` → target) → {id, selected: [..]}

vectorcraft.label: Paste Remembers Layers
vectorcraft.params: {on?} (default: toggle) the document option: on, the Paste commands put objects back into the layers they were copied from (by name; a missing one is made on top), off into the current layer; one undo step when it changes (document.inspect → pasteRemembersLayers) → {on}

vectorcraft.label: Merge Selected
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) merge two or more rows into the layer listed (highlighted) last: the other layers' contents and the other rows move into it, keeping their stacking order, and the emptied layers go. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one merged into a hidden or locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Flatten Artwork
vectorcraft.params: {id?} (default: the highlighted row's top-level layer, else the current one's) move the art of every other visible top-level layer into this one, keeping the stacking order; hidden layers and their art are deleted, template layers stay. Every selected object left hidden or locked, such as one flattened into a locked layer, is deselected (the key object too). One undo step → {id, discarded}

vectorcraft.label: Release to Layers (Sequence)
vectorcraft.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the highlighted row, else the current layer), build?: bool} each object in it goes into a new sublayer of its own, in stacking order (a group's objects go into sublayers of its layer, where the group was). `build`: Release to Layers (Build), each new sublayer holds copies of the objects up to its own, so the layers add up. One undo step → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Release to Layers (Build)
vectorcraft.params: {id?} layer.releaseToLayers with build: true → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Reverse Order
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} (default: the highlighted rows) reverse the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group; each keeps the places the others held. One undo step

vectorcraft.label: Template
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool (default: toggle the first)} make layers templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or ordinary layers again (layer.setProps template) → {on}

vectorcraft.label: Hide Others
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} hide every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which show. One undo step → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Show All Layers
vectorcraft.params: {} show every layer and sublayer → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Outline Others
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} turn Preview off (outline view) for every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which preview → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Preview All Layers
vectorcraft.params: {} turn Preview on for every layer and sublayer → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Lock Others
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} lock every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer), which unlock → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Unlock All Layers
vectorcraft.params: {} unlock every layer and sublayer → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Locate Object
vectorcraft.params: {id?} (default: the last selected object) highlight the object's row; the Layers panel opens the layers around it and scrolls to it → {id, ancestry: [layer…, id]}

vectorcraft.label: Pencil
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…] or [[x,y,pressure]…] (pen pressure 0..1: the stroke keeps it, for Calligraphic brushes with Pressure variation; a point without one presses fully), fidelity?: pt (1.5), closed?, style?: "pencil"|"brush", fill?: bool, keepSelected?: bool (true: the drawn or continued path is selected; false: it is not, and the rest of the selection stays), extend?: {id, end: "start"|"end"}, redraw?: {id, within?: pt (12)}} fit a freehand stroke → {id}. extend continues the path from that end; redraw (Edit Selected Paths) replaces the section of the path between where the stroke starts and ends, each within `within` of one subpath (the shorter way round a closed one), and draws a new path when the stroke doesn't end on it

vectorcraft.label: Curvature
vectorcraft.params: {points: [{x, y, corner?}], closed?, id?} create (or with id: replace) a path curving through the points → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Curvature
vectorcraft.params: {id, subpath?, op: "move"|"insert"|"extend"|"close", anchor?, segment?, t?, end?: "start"|"end", from?: "keep"|"smooth"|"corner", corner?, x?, y?} edit a path as the Curvature tool does, its shape kept elsewhere; the anchor edited becomes the direct-selected one → {anchor}. move: anchor to x, y, re-curving only its two segments (a smooth anchor takes the Curvature tool's handles, along the circle through it and its neighbours); insert: a smooth anchor at t on segment, the shape unchanged (with x, y: then moved there); extend: an open subpath goes on from its end (default) or start to a new end at x, y, curving into it unless corner is true; close: an open subpath closes from that end. The old end bends into the new segment as from says: keep its curve (default), smooth through its neighbours, or a corner

vectorcraft.label: Delete Anchor Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, subpath?, anchor} remove one anchor, re-fitting the curve

vectorcraft.label: Remove Anchor Points
vectorcraft.params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curve round each; the anchor after each removed one is selected, so running it again goes on along the path → {removedObjects}

vectorcraft.label: Convert Anchor Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, subpath?, anchor, to: "corner"|"smooth", x?, y?} (smooth with x/y: out handle there, in handle mirrored; without: as the Curvature tool curves a point, along the circle through it and its neighbours, or at an open end one handle into the curve)

vectorcraft.label: Reshape Segment
vectorcraft.params: {id, subpath?, segment, t, dx, dy, perpendicular?: bool} bend a segment so the point at t moves by (dx, dy); with perpendicular (Shift), both handles stand at right angles to the line between its anchors at one length, and the point at t lies as far from that line as the moved point does

vectorcraft.label: Split Path
vectorcraft.params: {id, subpath?, segment, t} or {id, subpath?, anchor}: closed paths open there, open paths become two → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Knife
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…]} cut closed shapes (selected, or all when nothing is selected) along the polyline → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Eraser
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…], size?: pt (10)} erase a round-brush stroke from paths (selected, or all) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Path Eraser
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…], width?: pt (8)} erase the parts of selected paths under the drag → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Smooth
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…], radius?: pt (12), fidelity?: pt (2.5)} smooth selected paths near the drag → {ids, before, after}

vectorcraft.label: Join
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…], tolerance?: pt (12)} join the open-path endpoints scrubbed over → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Blob Brush
vectorcraft.params: {points: [[x,y]…], size?: pt (10), merge?: true, mergeOnlySelection?: bool (false: merge with any touching same-color blob; true: only with selected ones), keepSelected?: bool (false: the drawn or merged path is not selected, and the rest of the selection stays; true: it is selected)} filled brush shape, merged with touching same-colour blobs → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Free Distort
vectorcraft.params: {corners: [[x,y]×4] (TL, TR, BR, BL), from?: [x0,y0,x1,y1] (default: selection bounds), ids?} projective warp of anchors and handles

vectorcraft.label: Sample Color
vectorcraft.params: {color, stroke?: bool (default: whichever proxy is active), ids?, stop?: index} sample a colour into the active fill/stroke (and the selection); with `stop`, recolour that stop of the gradient behind the proxy instead (paint.editGradient); in a CMYK document an RGB color is stored as CMYK through the color settings, as paint.setFill stores it

vectorcraft.label: Eyedropper Options
vectorcraft.params: {sampleSize?: 1|3|5 (pixels square averaged when sampling an image: point, 3×3, 5×5), pickUp?, apply?: {appearance?: {transparency?, fill?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?}, stroke?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?, weight?, cap?, join?, miter?, dash?}}, character?, paragraph?} (bools; a bool for a branch sets all of it)} Eyedropper Options, kept in the preferences: what appearance.copyFrom picks up from the clicked object and applies (only attributes in both trees are copied; every fill and stroke attribute copies the whole appearance stack); {} reads them → the options

vectorcraft.label: Move Artboard
vectorcraft.params: {index | indices: [index…], dx, dy, moveArt?: bool, copy?: bool, patterns?: bool (Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles)} move artboards (and the art fully inside them; locked and hidden art, and art also on another locked artboard, only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard), several in one step (an error when one is locked); `copy` (Alt-drag) leaves them and moves copies, which start unlocked → {index (the first), indices: the artboards moved or the copies, moved: the art moved or the copies}

vectorcraft.label: Apply Effect
vectorcraft.params: {effect: id (see effect.list, e.g. "stylize.dropShadow", "distort.roughen", "warp.arc", or "plugin.<id>" for an installed effect plug-in), params?: {…} (missing keys take the dialog defaults), item?: appearance item index|null (apply to that fill/stroke only; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item, else the whole object), ids?|id?: [..] (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents" (contents: the objects inside groups and layers)} append a live effect to each selected object's appearance (a group's or layer's apply to its members as one piece: one combined shadow; a Pathfinder effect, which combines a group's contents, groups several loose selected objects first, in the same undo step) → {ids, index, item, grouped?}

vectorcraft.label: Effects
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?: object ids (default: the selection), target?: "object"|"contents"} → {catalog: [{id, label, menu, params, defaults, raster, lengths: {always, absolute (while relative is false)} (distance params Scale Strokes & Effects scales)}] (installed effect plug-ins last: id plugin.<plug-in id>, menu Effect › Plug-ins), applied: [{id, effects, items: [{index, kind: fill|stroke, effects}]}], activeItem} for the selection

vectorcraft.label: Remove Effect
vectorcraft.params: {index: int (position in the effect list), item?: appearance item index|null (that fill/stroke's effects; omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents"} → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Effect Options
vectorcraft.params: {index: int, params?: {…} (merged into the current parameters), warpStyle?: string (an existing Warp style suffix, e.g. arc or flag; changes only an applied Warp in place), visible?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents"} → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: 3D Lighting Preset
vectorcraft.params: {index: int, preset: standard|diffuse|topLeft|right, item?: appearance item index|null (omitted: the active item, else the object's), ids?|id?: [..], target?: object|contents} replace an applied 3D effect's light rig and ambient with an original lighting preset; preserve shading, geometry and view; all targets must have a 3D effect at index; one undo step → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Expand Appearance
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?: [..], target?} turn each object's appearance into objects: every fill and stroke becomes an object of its own (strokes outlined, brushed strokes their brush art) grouped in paint order under the object's id and transparency, geometry effects are baked, raster effects become an embedded image (shadows and outer glows below the art; blur, feather and inner glow replace it; an object whose only raster effect is its own Rasterize becomes the image object.rasterize makes with the effect's options), type with effects or fills of its own is outlined; Crop Marks become a group of the object and its marks; a group's or layer's own fills and strokes become objects among its members, which are expanded too. Hidden fills, strokes and effects are dropped. Enabled when a selected or targeted object's appearance isn't basic (`ids` then pick which objects) → {ids, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

vectorcraft.label: Duplicate Effect
vectorcraft.params: {index: int, item?: appearance item index|null (as effect.remove), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents"} insert a copy of the effect right after it → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Move Effect
vectorcraft.params: {from: int (position in the source list), to: int (its position in the destination list afterwards), fromItem?: appearance item index|null (the source list: that fill/stroke's effects, null the object's; omitted: the active item, else the object's), toItem?: item index|null (the destination list; default: the source list), copy?: bool (copy instead of move, as Alt-dragging the row), ids?|id?: [..], target?: "object"|"contents"} reorder an effect or move it between the object and its fills/strokes, as one undo step → {ids, index, item}

vectorcraft.label: Unite
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Minus Front
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Intersect
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Exclude
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Divide
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Trim
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Merge
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Crop
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Outline
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Minus Back
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: [id…] (selected first; default: the selection)} operate on the selected objects (back → front) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Outline Stroke
vectorcraft.params: {} replace stroked paths with filled outlines → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Offset Path…
vectorcraft.params: {offset: pt (negative insets), joins?: "miter"|"round"|"bevel", miterLimit?: 4} → {ids} (new objects above the originals)

vectorcraft.label: Simplify…
vectorcraft.params: {tolerance?: pt (1), level?: 0..100 (the Simplify slider, in place of tolerance: 0 fewest anchor points, 50 is 1 pt, every 10 levels halves or doubles it), auto?: bool (Auto-Simplify: the lowest level whose tolerance is at most 1/400 of the selection's longer side, or 100 when that side is under 12.5 pt), cornerAngle?: deg (30), straightLines?: bool} → {ids, before, after} anchor counts, and the level used with level or auto

vectorcraft.label: Divide Objects Below
vectorcraft.params: {} cut the objects below with the selected path (which is removed) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Split Into Grid…
vectorcraft.params: {rows?: 2, columns?: 2, gutter?: pt (12; rowGutter?, columnGutter?: one of the two), totalHeight?, totalWidth?: pt (the grid's size; the selected paths' when left out), height?, width?: pt (each row's and column's size, which then sets the total), addGuides?: false (ruler guides along the row and column edges)} one grid of rectangles over the selected paths replaces them, painted as the topmost one → {ids, guides: count}

vectorcraft.label: Clean Up…
vectorcraft.params: {strayPoints?: true, unpaintedObjects?: true, emptyTextPaths?: true} → {removed}

vectorcraft.label: Vertical
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} set vertical writing

vectorcraft.label: Horizontal
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} set horizontal writing

vectorcraft.label: Create Outlines
vectorcraft.params: {} convert the selected text to groups of compound paths (one per glyph) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Scale Text Attributes
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} bake each selected type object's transform scale into its character sizes (leading, baseline shift and horizontal scale included), leaving rotation and position in the affine → {ids, changed}

vectorcraft.label: Optical Margin Alignment
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Optical Margin Alignment on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting): in every paragraph of point and area type, quotation marks, hyphens, full stops and commas at a line's start or end hang wholly outside the margin there; asterisks, tildes, ellipses, en and em dashes, colons and semicolons hang by half; and A, V, W, Y, v, w and y hang by a tenth of their advance; a left-aligned line hangs at its left margin, a right-aligned line hangs at its right margin, and centered and justified lines hang at both; Auto aligns a right-to-left line at its right; type on a path hangs at the start bracket when its line is placed there, hangs at the end bracket when the line is placed there, and hangs at both when it is centered → {on, ids}

vectorcraft.label: System Layout
vectorcraft.params: {on?: bool} turn System Layout on or off for the document (on omitted: the opposite of the document's setting) and every text object in it. On, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. Off (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing uses fractions of a point. New point, area and path type inherits the document's setting → {on}

vectorcraft.label: Fractional Widths
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, on?: bool} turn Fractional Widths on or off for the selected type and every frame of its threads (on omitted: the opposite of the first object's setting). On (the default, and what a document from before it reads as), spacing between characters uses fractions of a point. Off, each character that takes any space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together; a character with no width stays at none. The setting is the whole type object, not a range of characters → {on, ids}

vectorcraft.label: Set Text
vectorcraft.params: {id?|ids?, text} replace the contents of text objects (keeps the first run's style) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits)}

vectorcraft.label: Area Type Options…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, width?: pt, height?: pt, rows?, columns?, gutter?: pt, inset?: pt, firstBaseline?: ascent|capHeight|xHeight|leading|fixed, firstBaselineMin?: pt, verticalAlign?: top|center|bottom|justify, fit?: none|autoHeight|shrinkText, fitMinPercent?: 10..100, …the keys of its own reply (it can be passed back; the values it only reports are ignored)} set the selected area type's options; width and height size the type area from its top-left corner, along the type's own axes, and the text reflows at its size (with fit autoHeight, Auto Size, the frame's height follows the text after every edit and height is ignored; setting the height by hand turns it off); fit shrinkText scales overflowing text down (size, leading, baseline shift) by the largest factor down to fitMinPercent % (default 50) that makes it fit (none given: query) → the first object's options, plus overflow (the text doesn't fit its frame) and fitScale (Shrink Text's factor, 1 unshrunk)

vectorcraft.label: Reshape Type Area
vectorcraft.params: {id, anchors: [[subpath, anchor]…], dx, dy} move anchors of area type's frame (the type area) by dx, dy points, with their handles; the text reflows at its size, through its thread too (what Direct Selection does dragging a frame corner or edge)

vectorcraft.label: Fit Headline
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} track the first line of area type so it fills the frame width → {tracking}

vectorcraft.label: Character
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, font?, style?, size?: pt, leading?: pt|"auto", tracking?: 1/1000 em, justify?: "auto" (the start of each paragraph's direction)|"left"|"center"|"right"|"justifyAll", fill?: colour, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), features?: ["dlig", "-liga", …] OpenType, start?: byte, end?: byte} (size/leading are document points after object scaling; with a range: the character attributes style that range and justify the paragraphs it touches; without: all the text) → {ids, overflow?: [id…] (area type and type on a path whose text no longer fits; left out when all fits)}

vectorcraft.label: Ruby…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, start?: byte, end?: byte, text?: reading, position?: above|below (vertical type: right|left), align?: start|center|end, size?: 1–100 (percent of the base text's size, default 50), overhang?: bool (default true), remove?: bool} set the ruby (furigana) over the selected text's bytes in `start..end` (without them: all its text): the reading over the base characters, above them in horizontal type and right of them in vertical type; `remove` takes the ruby off the range instead → {ids, ruby: [{start, end, text, position, align, sizePercent, overhang}…] (the first object's ruby)}

vectorcraft.label: All Artwork Above
vectorcraft.params: {} lock objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left locked or hidden (the key object too) → {count}

vectorcraft.label: Other Layers
vectorcraft.params: {} lock every layer that holds no selected object → {count}

vectorcraft.label: All Artwork Above
vectorcraft.params: {} hide objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection, deselecting every selected object left hidden or locked (the key object too) → {count}

(with trim), warning? (without trim: the image couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

vectorcraft.params: {ids?, steps?: n | distance?: pt | smooth?: bool, orientation?: page|path (default: the Blend Options set with nothing selected, else smooth colour and page), starts?: [anchor index | null, …] (per object of `ids`, else of the selection in paint order: the anchor of its first subpath the blend starts from; an open path's last anchor runs it the other way), spacing?: smooth|steps|distance (with value), value?: n, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct (0..100), colorShift?: pct (-100..100; 0: even)} blend the selected objects (paint order) into a live blend; a blend among them takes the others in as more key objects (keeping its options, name and transparency) instead of nesting → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Release
vectorcraft.params: {} release the selected blends: the key objects come back and the spine stays as a path with no fill or stroke, below them; a blend with a name, opacity, blend mode, isolation, opacity mask or appearance of its own comes back as a group keeping them (and its knockout) → {ids (the keys), spines: [ids], groups: [ids]}

vectorcraft.label: Blend Options…
vectorcraft.params: {spacing?: smooth|steps|distance, value?: n, steps?: n, distance?: pt, orientation?: page|path, smooth?: bool, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct} set the options of the selected blends; easingType chooses the distribution, ramp sets its strength (0..100; 0 = even), colorShift (-100..100; 0 = even) shifts colours independently of shape/position easing (omitted ones keep their value; out of range is an error); with no blend selected, the options new blends start with (spacing and orientation only; a tool setting, not an undo step) → {defaults?: true}

vectorcraft.label: Expand
vectorcraft.params: {} replace the selected blends by groups of their keys and steps, each keeping the blend's id, name, transparency (knockout and isolation included), opacity mask and appearance → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Replace Spine
vectorcraft.params: {} use the selected path as the spine of the selected blend (the path is consumed)

vectorcraft.label: Reverse Spine
vectorcraft.params: {} reverse the order of the key objects along the spine

vectorcraft.params: {} the options of the first selected blend, else those new blends start with → {target: blend|defaults, id?, spacing: smooth|steps|distance, steps, distance, orientation: page|path, easingType?: easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|easeOutIn, ramp?: pct, colorShift?: pct, keys?: [ids], starts?: [anchor|null], spine?: {anchors: [{x, y, in: [x, y], out: [x, y]}], closed, keyAnchors: [anchor each key sits on] | null (keys spread evenly: a spine from Replace Spine), explicit: false for the straight lines between the key centres}}

vectorcraft.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, x, y, handle?: in|out, independent?: bool} move a point of the blend's spine (its handles along), or with `handle` place that handle's end at (x, y) (a smooth point keeps the other handle in line unless `independent`). A key object sitting on the point moves with it. The first edit turns the straight spine into a path

vectorcraft.label: Convert Anchor Point
vectorcraft.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, to: smooth|corner, x?, y?} convert a blend spine point: dragging a corner creates symmetric smooth handles, clicking a point with handles retracts both. Without x/y, smooth uses the neighbouring spine points

vectorcraft.label: Reshape Spine Segment

vectorcraft.label: Delete Spine Point

vectorcraft.label: Reverse Front to Back
vectorcraft.params: {} reverse the stacking order of the selected blends

vectorcraft.label: Make with Mesh…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?, rows?: 1..50 (4), cols?: 1..50 (4), columns?: as cols} envelope the selected objects with a mesh of rows × cols patches → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Make with Top Object
vectorcraft.params: {ids?} the topmost selected path becomes the envelope of the others → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Reset with Warp…

vectorcraft.label: Reset with Mesh…
vectorcraft.params: {rows?: 1..50, cols?: 1..50 (unset: a mesh envelope's own, else 4), maintainShape?: bool (true: the mesh follows the current envelope shape; false: a flat grid over the content), columns?: as cols} make the selected envelopes mesh envelopes, keeping their content

vectorcraft.label: Envelope Info
vectorcraft.params: {} the selected envelope's settings, or with none selected the defaults new envelopes get → {id: n|null, type: warp|mesh|topObject, style, bend, h, v, horizontal, rows, cols, fidelity, antiAlias, preserveShape: clippingMask|transparency, distortAppearance, distortLinearGradients, distortPatternFills, editing}

vectorcraft.label: Release
vectorcraft.params: {} release the selected envelopes into their content and their shape (a grey gradient mesh for warp and mesh envelopes, the path for a top-object envelope; the content keeps the envelope's opacity, blend mode and opacity mask) → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Envelope Options…
vectorcraft.params: {fidelity?: 0..100, antiAlias?: bool, preserveShape?: clippingMask|transparency, distortAppearance?: bool, distortLinearGradients?: bool, distortPatternFills?: bool (the last two work with distortAppearance), style?, bend?, h?, v?, horizontal? (warp envelopes), horizontalDistortion?: as h, verticalDistortion?: as v, orientation?: horizontal|vertical} set the selected envelopes' options; with no envelope selected, the options new envelopes get (see object.envelope.info)

vectorcraft.label: Expand
vectorcraft.params: {} replace the selected envelopes by groups of their distorted content (type outlined), keeping name, opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout and opacity mask → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Edit Contents
vectorcraft.params: {editing?: bool} toggle Edit Contents / Edit Envelope → {editing}

vectorcraft.label: Move Envelope Mesh Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, index, x, y, handle?: 0 right|1 left|2 down|3 up} move a point of a mesh envelope (its handles follow), or with `handle` place that handle end at (x, y); object.mesh.movePoint, addLine and deletePoint edit mesh envelopes too

vectorcraft.label: Create Gradient Mesh…
vectorcraft.params: {ids?, rows?: n (4), cols?: n (4), appearance?: flat|center|edge, highlight?: % (100), at?: [x,y], columns?: as cols} convert filled paths into gradient meshes in their fill colour (a gradient fill: the colour it paints at each point), lightened per `appearance` (with `at`: 1×1 mesh plus lines through that point); an embedded image becomes a mesh over its rectangle (its transform kept) whose points take the average colour and opacity of the picture around them (a linked image is refused: embed it first) → {ids, index?}

vectorcraft.params: {id, index, color, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1} colour of one mesh point

vectorcraft.params: {id, index, x, y, handle?: 0 right|1 left|2 down|3 up} move a point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope (its handles follow), or with `handle` place that handle end at (x, y)

vectorcraft.params: {id? (default: the one selected type object), start?: byte, end?: byte (default: all text), font?, style?, size?: pt, leading?: pt|"auto", tracking?, kerning?: 1/1000 em|"auto", baselineShift?: pt, hScale?: %, vScale?: %, rotation?: deg, fill?: colour|"none", stroke?: colour|"none", keepModel?: bool (fill and stroke, as paint.setFill), strokeWidth?: pt, strokeOptions?: {weight?, cap?, join?, miterLimit?, align?, dash?, dashOffset?, alignDashes?} (as stroke.set: the character stroke), underline?, strikethrough?, allCaps?: bool, smallCaps?: bool, position?: "normal"|"superscript"|"subscript" (sizes from Document Setup), features?: ["dlig", "-liga", …], charAlign?: "romanBaseline"|"emBoxTop"|"emBoxCenter"|"emBoxBottom"|"icfTop"|"icfBottom", proportionalMetrics?: bool (full-width glyphs on the font's proportional widths: `palt` in horizontal type, `vpal` in vertical type), tateChuYoko?: bool (Character panel menu › Tate-chu-yoko, with Show East Asian Options: in vertical type those characters stand side by side across one em of the column; kept on the characters and ignored in horizontal type), noBreak?: bool (Character panel menu › No Break: these characters stay on one line, including across a space inside the run), charDirection?: "default"|"leftToRight"|"rightToLeft" (Character panel menu › Character Direction: the characters are set left to right or right to left inside their paragraph, as a Unicode bidi embedding; default: as the bidi algorithm sets them), digits?: "default"|"arabic"|"hindi"|"farsi" (Character panel menu › Digits: the numeral system every digit is drawn in, whatever was typed), fontAxes?: {"wght": 650, …} (Character panel › Variable Font: the setting of each variation axis named, in the axis's units and clamped to its range; null: back to the style's own setting; other axes keep theirs; tags the font has no axis for are left out; a font or style change clears them; text.fontList {family, style} lists the axes)} style a character range (size/leading/baselineShift are document points and hScale includes the object transform; runs are split at the range ends) → {id, runs}

vectorcraft.label: Touch Type
vectorcraft.params: {id, start: byte (a character of it), dx?: pt, dy?: pt, hScale?: %, vScale?: %, rotation?: deg} change one character (a ligature, one glyph for several characters, as a whole) as a Touch Type tool drag does, as one undo step: dx moves it along its line in reading order by changing the kerning of the character before it on the line and its own kerning, and the characters after it stay where they are (an error for the first character of a line and for a right-to-left character; limited to what kerning from -1000 to 10000 can give); dy raises it (baseline shift, along its own up axis when it is rotated); dx and dy are document points; hScale (including the object transform), vScale and rotation set its scales and rotation as text.setRangeStyle does. The kerning of the two characters also keeps the character and the ones after it where they were along the line when the font kerned them with their neighbors; a wider or narrower character moves the ones after it by the change in its width → {id, start, end} (the character's bytes)

Preferences › Type › Show Font Names in English only changes the UI menu labels, not this list; with family: {family, styles: [names] (upright styles by weight, then italics; an error when the family isn't available), axes: [{tag, name, min, default, max, value, hidden}] (a variable font's variation axes, the Character panel's Variable Font sliders, with `value` the setting of `style`, else of the first style; empty for a static font; `hidden`: the font asks for the axis not to be shown)}

CSS generic families such as sans-serif and names longer than 256 bytes are left out. fontsNextToDocument: the Fonts folder next to the saved document (File › Package writes it), when there is one and a search may start there (not in another app's folders, such as a mail app's attachments)

vectorcraft.label: Find Font Files
vectorcraft.params: {folder?: an absolute path, fonts?: [{family, style?}] (1 to 1000; default: the active document's missing fonts, as text.missingFonts lists them), maxSeconds?: 60 (1 to 600), stop?: false (true: stop the last search)} with folder: look in it and its subfolders for font files that make the fonts available, on separate threads, and answer at once (state: searching); without folder: the last search's state, with the files found so far. A search reads the table directories and the name, fvar and OS/2 tables of .ttf, .otf, .ttc and .otc files of at most 256 MB and, on macOS, of suitcase fonts (files without an extension or with .suit, whose fonts are in a resource fork of at most 8 MB), and lists a file for a font when the file, added with text.addFontFiles, makes the font resolve exactly as text.fonts resolves it; fonts that resolve exactly already are left out. It doesn't enter app packages, folders named Program Files (also x86 and Arm), ProgramData, $Recycle.Bin or System Volume Information, the system's folders at the root of a volume, the Shared and Public folders in Users, a home folder's Library, AppData, Applications, snap and dot folders, a Library folder's app data folders or the folders the environment names for apps' data, and a search of a folder inside one of them fails; the walk also skips other hidden folders, folders whose contents are in the cloud and folders more than 64 levels deep, and follows no links (a picked path is resolved through its links); none on the web → {id (absent while idle), state: idle|searching|done|stopped|failed, folder?, fonts: [{family, style, status, files: [paths]}], searched?: {folders, files, fontFiles}, skipped?, unreadable?, stopped?: stop|time|limit, error?, seconds?}

vectorcraft.label: Add Font Files
vectorcraft.params: {files: [paths the last text.findFontFiles search found] (1 to 1000)} copy the font files into VectorCraft's own Fonts folder (next to the preferences; the desktop app and vectorcraft-cli read it), never replacing a file there: the names Name.otf, Name 2.otf … Name 99.otf are tried in turn until one is free, which gets the copy, or is a file with the same contents, which is kept; then scan the fonts again, as text.rescanFonts does, and type set in them redraws. Only regular .ttf, .otf, .ttc, .otc, .woff and .woff2 files and suitcase fonts (with their resource fork) are copied, at most 256 MB a file and 1 GB in all; any other file is skipped. Add only fonts you own or are licensed to install; none on the web → {folder, copied: [{from, to}], kept: [{from, to}], skipped: [{file, reason}], families?, faces?}

vectorcraft.params: {id?: Intertwine group (default: the selected one), at?: [x,y] (the overlap area under this point, as a click picks it) | area?: [[x,y]…] (a closed polygon drawn around overlap areas: every area whose inside it encloses), order?: toggle|front|back (toggle: the object drawn right below the top comes to the front, so two objects swap), member?: id (front and back: the object to move; default: front brings the object right below the top, back sends the top one)} → {count: areas changed, top: [id of the object now on top in each area]}

vectorcraft.label: Attach
vectorcraft.params: {path?: id of the path to attach to (without it: choose the Objects on Path tool, whose click on a path attaches the selection to it), ids?: the objects to attach (default: the selection; the path is left out of it), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; default 4, the center), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path (default 0)} put the objects and the path in an Objects on Path group: the path at the bottom, the objects spread evenly along it from its first anchor (the last one at the end of an open path) in their order on the canvas, column by column from left to right and top to bottom in each column, each turned to follow the path; editing the path moves them → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Objects on Path Options
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection), pivot?: 0-8 (the reference point of each object that attaches to the path, row by row from the top left; 4: the center), rotate?: degrees counter-clockwise from upright on the path} set how the objects of the groups attach → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Expand
vectorcraft.params: {ids?: Objects on Path groups or objects in them (default: the selection)} make the groups plain groups of the path and the objects where they are → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Get Preferences
vectorcraft.params: {key?} → the value of one preference (or preference group: eyedropper), or {prefs: {…all…}}

vectorcraft.label: Set Preference
vectorcraft.params: {key, value} or {values: {key: value, …}} set preferences (validated; see prefs.list; lengths in pt or strings with a unit; unitsGeneral also sets the active document's units, one undo step; the eyedropper group takes a partial object, as eyedropper.setOptions)

vectorcraft.label: Reset Preferences
vectorcraft.params: {category?} reset one category (or everything) to defaults

vectorcraft.label: List Preferences
vectorcraft.params: {} → [{key, category, section, label, kind, value, …}] every preference

vectorcraft.label: Width Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, t: 0..1 (fraction of the path length), left, right: side widths in pt, index?: width point to edit or move, adjustAdjoining?: bool (the nearest points either side change their widths in proportion, using the sampled widths for a new point)} → {index}. Without index a point already at t is replaced; a point moved onto another one's t joins it as a discontinuous point (on the side it came from), so the width steps there. Creates a uniform profile first if needed

vectorcraft.label: Delete Width Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, index | indices: [..]} remove width points (removing the last one leaves a uniform stroke)

vectorcraft.label: Copy Width Point
vectorcraft.params: {id, index: the width point to copy, t: 0..1 where the copy goes} → {index} (Alt-drag with the Width tool). Landing on another point makes a discontinuous point, as a stroke.widthPoint.set move does

vectorcraft.label: Width Profile
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, points: [[t, left, right]…] (width factors, 1 = the stroke weight) | null = uniform}

vectorcraft.label: Liquify
vectorcraft.params: {tool: warp|twirl|pucker|bloat|scallop|crystallize|wrinkle, points: [[x,y,pressure?]…] (the brush stroke; pen pressure 0..1, default 1), diameter?|width?, height? (pt, default 100), angle?, intensity? (0..1 or %), usePressure?: bool (each point's pressure is the intensity there), detail? (1..10), simplify?: 0..100, simplifyOn?: bool (default true; both for warp, twirl, pucker, bloat), rate? (twirl °), complexity? (0..15), horizontal?, vertical? (wrinkle, 0..1 or %), affectAnchors?, affectIn?, affectOut?: bool (scallop, crystallize, wrinkle; default true), ids?|id? (default: selection, else every path the brush touches)}

vectorcraft.label: Puppet Warp
vectorcraft.params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), pins: [[x,y]…] (current pin positions), moved: [[x,y]…] (targets, same length), angles?: [deg|null…] (same length: the turn the art takes around each pin, as Alt-dragging around a pin does; null leaves it free), expand?: pt, rest?: bool, auto?: bool (as object.puppetWarp.pins reports; ignored)} as-rigid-as-possible mesh warp of anchors and handles. rest: true = the Puppet Warp tool's pins: `pins` are points on the shape the pins started from (object.puppetWarp.pins), each must be on its mesh, the warp replaces the previous one instead of adding to it, and the pins are kept with the document for Undo (an empty list removes them all, leaving the art as it is)

vectorcraft.label: Puppet Warp Pins
vectorcraft.params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), expand?: pt} → {ids, pins, moved, angles, expand, rest: true, auto} the Puppet Warp pins on the art: pins = where each sits on the shape they started from, moved = where it is now, angles = the turn it holds (deg, null = free); auto: none placed yet (the tool's automatic pins: the centre and the end of each limb). Change moved/angles (or add/remove pins) and pass it back to object.puppetWarp

vectorcraft.label: Define Perspective Grid
vectorcraft.params: {kind?: 1|2|3, origin?: [x,y], horizon?, vpLeft?, vpRight?, vpVertical?: [x,y], distance?, cell?, extent?, height?, visible?, plane?, leftOffset?, rightOffset?, groundOffset?: pt (planes moved along their normals), reproject?: bool, …the other fields of the grid as its reply lists them} merge into the document's grid. Objects in perspective stay where they are, as in the reference app; with reproject they move with the grid (each keeps its place on its plane)

vectorcraft.label: Perspective Grid Preset
vectorcraft.params: {kind: 1|2|3 (its normal view) | name: a preset (see perspective.presets.list)} reset the grid to the preset fitted to the first artboard (and show it; attached objects stay attached)

vectorcraft.label: Show Perspective Grid
vectorcraft.params: {visible?: bool} (no param toggles). View state: not an undo step

vectorcraft.label: Active Perspective Plane
vectorcraft.params: {plane: left|right|ground|none} Plane Switching widget. View state: not an undo step

vectorcraft.label: Attach to Active Plane
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane)} project the objects onto the plane

vectorcraft.label: Release with Perspective
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} detach from the grid (geometry unchanged)

vectorcraft.label: Move in Perspective
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, from: [x,y], to: [x,y], plane?, copy?: bool (move copies, as Alt-dragging does), perpendicular?: bool (move along the plane's normal instead, as pressing 5 while dragging does), snap?: bool (default: View › Perspective Grid › Snap to Grid)} slide objects within their plane (unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); snapping lands the nearer edge of the objects' joint bounds on a gridline within a quarter cell; Transform Again repeats it

vectorcraft.label: Draw in Perspective
vectorcraft.params: {command: shape.* id, params, plane?, snap?: bool (default: Snap to Grid), at?: [x, y] (a point of the plane the shape lies on, as the tool gives it)} run a shape command and attach the result to the plane (snapping its corners to gridlines within a quarter cell)

vectorcraft.label: Transform in Perspective
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f] (affine map in plane coordinates, points: u along the plane, v up or away), depth?: pt to move along the plane's normal (default 0), copy?: bool, plane?} transform objects within their own planes (Perspective Selection tool handles; unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); Transform Again repeats it → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Nudge in Perspective
vectorcraft.params: {dx, dy: arrow direction (-1, 0 or 1), big?: bool (×10), copy?: bool} move the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Move Plane
vectorcraft.params: {plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane), offset?: pt (where along its normal; 0 is its place in the grid's definition) | by?: pt, objects?: none|move|copy (default none: the objects on the plane stay; move: they move with it, as Shift-dragging a plane widget does; copy: copies of them do, as Alt-dragging does)} → {plane, offset, ids}

vectorcraft.label: Move Plane to Match Object
vectorcraft.params: {id? (default: the first selected object)} move the plane the object is attached to onto the object and make it the active plane → {plane, offset}

vectorcraft.label: Edit Text
vectorcraft.params: {id? (default: the selected type)} Object › Perspective › Edit Text: show type in perspective flat where it is drawn, in isolation mode, to edit it (text.* commands, the Type tool); exiting isolation (object.exitIsolation, Esc) projects it again → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Invert
vectorcraft.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} invert the active proxy's colours of the selection (or ids; groups recolour their contents) keeping each colour's model, as edit.colors.invert does; the Appearance panel's active fill/stroke item (appearance.setActiveItem) is inverted instead when it is of that kind and no ids are given; with nothing selected, invert the default → {changed}

vectorcraft.label: Complement
vectorcraft.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} replace the active proxy's colours by their complements ((highest + lowest) − each component, over RGB or CMY; grey unchanged) keeping each colour's model; honours the Appearance panel's active item as paint.invert does; with nothing selected, the default → {changed}

vectorcraft.label: Apply Last Color
vectorcraft.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last solid colour used (paint.recent lastColor) to the active proxy of the selection and the default

vectorcraft.label: Apply Last Gradient
vectorcraft.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy), ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} apply the last gradient used (paint.recent lastGradient), fitted to each object, to the active proxy of the selection and the default

vectorcraft.label: Recent Colors
vectorcraft.params: {} → {colors: [{hex, color}] newest first (fed by every paint command and the eyedropper), lastColor: {hex, color}, lastGradient: gradient paint}

vectorcraft.label: Fill and Stroke
vectorcraft.params: {} → {fill, stroke: the paints the Fill/Stroke proxies show (the Appearance panel's active item for the proxy of its kind, else the first selected object's, a group's first painted object's, type: its first run's; else the defaults for new art), fillActive, fillMixed, strokeMixed: the selected objects' (or a selected group's contents') fills (strokes) differ, shown as a "?" proxy}

vectorcraft.label: Overprint
vectorcraft.params: {fill?: bool, stroke?: bool, item?: appearance item index|null, ids?|id?, target?: "object"|"contents"} make fills and/or strokes overprint (Overprint Preview, Separations Preview) or knock out: item's, else every fill or stroke of the painted objects (groups: their contents; type: its characters too). Without item and ids, the Appearance panel's active item stands in when it is of that kind → {changed: objects}

vectorcraft.label: Attributes
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?, item?, target?: "object"|"contents"} → {ids, overprintFill, overprintStroke, showCenter, imageMap: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url, note, fillRule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd" (of the paths and compound paths in them), reversed (their subpaths run counter-clockwise on screen: Reverse Path Direction On), recentUrls: [newest first]} the Attributes panel's values for `ids` or the selection, overprint aimed as object.setOverprint aims; a value is null where they differ (or nothing has a fill, stroke or path)

vectorcraft.label: Swatch Libraries
vectorcraft.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"gradients"|"user" (User Defined: the library files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (swatch.library.load), count, path?}], userFolder} every library the library panel opens, in menu order

vectorcraft.label: Swatch Library
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, swatches: [{name, kind, group, global, spot, color?, hex?, gradient?}] (as swatch.list), groups: [{name, swatches: [names]}]}

vectorcraft.label: Add to Swatches
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name, names?: [swatch or colour group names in the library] (default: all of it; a group comes as a colour group, a single swatch ungrouped), apply?: "fill"|"stroke" (also apply the first one to the selection and the defaults, as paint.setFill / paint.setStroke), focus?: true (with apply: false keeps the active proxy)} copy library swatches into the document as one undo step. A swatch the document already has (same name and paint) isn't added again; a name taken by another swatch gets a number ("Clay 1 2") → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}

vectorcraft.label: Default Swatches
vectorcraft.params: {replace?: false} bring back the default swatches and colour groups of the document's colour mode that are missing (by name), as one undo step; replace: true makes the swatches exactly the defaults (art linked to a removed global swatch keeps its colour, unlinked) → {added: [names]}

vectorcraft.label: Save Swatch Library…
vectorcraft.params: {path?, format?: "vcswatches" (lossless JSON: colour models, global, spot, gradients, groups) | "gpl" (8-bit RGB palette; groups as `# Group:` comments) | "ase" (swatch exchange, binary: solid colors in their own model (RGB, CMYK, Lab, Gray) as global, spot or process colors, and color groups; gradients are left out, and a tint swatch is saved as the color it shows) | "css" (custom properties on :root) (default: the path's extension, else vcswatches), names?: [swatch or colour group names] (default: all; None and patterns are never saved), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's swatches as a library → {path, format, count: the swatches written (gpl and ase hold solid colors only, and css leaves freeform gradients out), library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, format, count}, or {dataBase64, format, count} for ase

vectorcraft.label: Other Library…
vectorcraft.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcswatches, .gpl, .ase (swatch exchange) or .acb (color book, read only) library, or the swatches of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Swatch Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same extension and bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

vectorcraft.label: Copy to User Defined
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name of a loaded library (category "loaded", swatch.library.load)} copy it into the user library folder of the desktop app, whose libraries VectorCraft lists as User Defined every time it starts (a loaded library is listed until the app quits): a library file as it is, the swatches of a document or a library loaded from data as a .vcswatches file. A name the folder already has gets a number ("Brand 2.ase") and no file is replaced; when the folder already holds the same file, that file is used. The library is then listed as User Defined only, and until the app quits commands given its loaded id use the copy; a User Defined library comes back as it is → {library: its User Defined id, name, count, path, copied: false when nothing was written}

vectorcraft.label: Add Freeform Point
vectorcraft.params: {at: [x,y] (document coordinates), color? (default: the gradient's colour there), keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %; the radius of pure colour around the point, a fraction of half the object's larger side; default 0), line?: true (join it to the selected point: extends the line ending there, else starts one), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} add a point to the freeform gradient (an unplaced one keeps its automatic points first) and select it → {index}

vectorcraft.label: Edit Freeform Point
vectorcraft.params: {index? (default: the selected point), at?: [x,y] (document coordinates), color?, keepModel?: bool (as paint.setFill), opacity?: 0..1 (or 0..100), spread?: 0..1 (or 0..100 %), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} move or recolour a point of the freeform gradient → {index}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Freeform Point
vectorcraft.params: {index? (default: the selected point), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} remove a point (never the last one); lines through it close up around it and lines left with one point go → {index}

vectorcraft.label: Add Freeform Line
vectorcraft.params: {points: [index, …] (at least two), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} join points with a smooth line through them, in order → {line}

vectorcraft.label: Split Freeform Line
vectorcraft.params: {line: line index, segment: the segment from the line's point `segment` to the next, t?: 0..1 along it (default 0.5), ids?|id?, stroke?: bool (default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy), item?: fill/stroke item index|null (omitted: the Appearance panel's active item when it is of the edited kind), target?: "object"|"contents"} add a point on a line there (colour, opacity and spread between the segment's ends) and select it → {index}

vectorcraft.label: Select Freeform Point
vectorcraft.params: {index: point index | null to clear} select a point of the freeform gradient behind the active proxy (the first selected object's): the point the Gradient tool, the Gradient and Color panels and Delete act on → {index}

vectorcraft.label: Freeform Gradient
vectorcraft.params: {stroke?: bool (default: the active proxy)} the freeform gradient behind the proxy of the first selected object → {mode: points|lines, points: [{at: [x,y] (document coordinates), color, opacity, spread}], lines: [[index, …]], selected: index|null}

vectorcraft.label: Flatten Transparency…
vectorcraft.params: {preset?: "high"|"medium"|"low" or a saved preset's name (see flattener.presets.list; default medium), balance?: 0..100 (raster/vector balance; 0 rasterizes everything), lineArtPpi?: 1..2400, gradientPpi?: 1..2400 (areas only gradients and meshes reach), textToOutlines?, strokesToOutlines?, clipComplexRegions? (clip images to the region outlines, else rectangles), antiAlias?, preserveAlpha? (composite over nothing instead of white), preserveOverprints? (areas showing one paint keep its colour and overprint; false clears overprints), options?: {the same keys}, ids?|id?} overlapping transparent objects become one group of flat-colour regions (CMYK colours composited ink by ink in CMYK documents), plus an image where gradients, patterns, images, masks or raster effects reach; objects without transparency stay → {ids, rasterized: images made, vector: regions made, options, warning? (an image in the art couldn't be decoded, as object.rasterize says)}

vectorcraft.label: Transparency Flattener Presets
vectorcraft.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, options}]} the built-in presets (High, Medium and Low Resolution), then the saved ones; any of these names works as `preset` wherever flattener options are taken

vectorcraft.label: Save Transparency Flattener Preset
vectorcraft.params: {name?: (default: a new "Flattener Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else medium), …options (the keys of object.flattenTransparency, at the top level or in `options`)} create or change a saved preset (built-in ones can't change) → {name, options, created}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Transparency Flattener Preset
vectorcraft.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}

vectorcraft.label: Import Transparency Flattener Presets
vectorcraft.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else the imported ones get a number)} add the presets of a .vcflattener file (as flattener.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}

vectorcraft.label: Export Transparency Flattener Presets
vectorcraft.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcflattener file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}

vectorcraft.label: Flattener Preview
vectorcraft.params: {highlight?: "none"|"rasterizedRegions" (areas the raster/vector balance rasterizes whole)|"transparentObjects"|"allAffected"|"expandedPatterns" (pattern art taking part)|"outlinedStrokes"|"outlinedText"|"allRasterized" (default none), overprints?: "preserve"|"simulate"|"discard" (simulate and discard flatten without preserveOverprints), preset?, …options as object.flattenTransparency, ids?|id?: (default: the whole document)} what flattening would do, without changing anything → {highlight, regions: [{bounds: {x, y, width, height}, id?}] (the highlighted objects, or areas), counts: {transparentObjects, allAffected, expandedPatterns, outlinedStrokes, outlinedText, rasterizedRegions, allRasterized, vectorRegions}, options}

vectorcraft.label: Graphic Style Libraries
vectorcraft.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"user" (User Defined: the .vcstyles files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (graphicStyle.loadLibrary), count, path?}], userFolder} every graphic style library the library panel opens, in menu order

vectorcraft.label: Graphic Style Library
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, styles: [{name, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fills, strokes, effects: [effect id…], opacity, blend, isolate, knockout}] (as graphicStyle.list)}

vectorcraft.label: Add to Graphic Styles
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name, name? | names?: [style names in the library] (default: all of it), apply?: false (also apply the first one to `ids` or the selection, if any, as graphicStyle.apply), add?: false (with apply: add its appearance on top, as Alt-click), ids?} copy library styles into the document's Graphic Styles as one undo step (with the apply). A style the document already has (same name and look) isn't added again; a name taken by another style gets a number ("Halo 2"). The patterns they paint with come along (a name taken by another pattern or swatch gets a number) → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}

vectorcraft.label: Save Graphic Style Library…
vectorcraft.params: {path?, names?: [style names] (default: all), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's graphic styles as a .vcstyles library (JSON: the styles, unlinked from swatches, and the patterns they paint with) → {path, count, library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, count}

vectorcraft.label: Other Library…
vectorcraft.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcstyles library, or the graphic styles of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Graphic Style Libraries lists it until the app quits; a file of the user library folder, or a file with the same extension and bytes as one there, opens as that User Defined library) → {library: id, name, count}

vectorcraft.label: Libraries
vectorcraft.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, graphics, colors, charStyles, paraStyles, groups} (counts)], current: the current library's id or null, folder: the library folder, or null when libraries last for the session only (the web, headless)}

vectorcraft.label: Library
vectorcraft.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library)} → {id, name, graphics: [{id, name, width, height, thumbnail: PNG base64}], colors: [{name, hex, color}], charStyles: [{name, attrs}], paraStyles: [{name, attrs}], groups: [{name, items: [{kind: color|charStyle|paraStyle|graphic, item: name (graphic: id)}]}] (an item is in one group at most; the others are ungrouped)}

vectorcraft.label: Show Library
vectorcraft.params: {library: id or name} the library the Libraries panel shows, which library commands without a `library` act on → {id}

vectorcraft.label: Create New Library
vectorcraft.params: {name?: "My Library"} a new empty library (its file in the library folder), made the current one → {id, name}

vectorcraft.label: Rename Library
vectorcraft.params: {library?, name} rename a library (default: the current one) → {id, name}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Library
vectorcraft.params: {library?} delete a library (default: the current one) and its file; not undoable → null

vectorcraft.label: Add to Library
vectorcraft.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library, made when there is none), kind: graphic|fillColor|strokeColor|charStyle|paraStyle, ids?: objects (default: the selection), name?, color?: colour (a colour to add, instead of the selection's)} add an item from the selection: graphic: a copy of the objects with every resource they use; fillColor/strokeColor: the first selected object's solid fill/stroke colour (else the default fill/stroke); charStyle/paraStyle: the selected text's character/paragraph attributes (the Type tool's range, else the first selected text object). An item the library already has (same kind and contents) isn't added again → {library, kind, name, id?: graphic id, existing: bool}

vectorcraft.label: Use Library Item
vectorcraft.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name), center?: [x, y] (graphic; default: the first artboard's centre), to?: fill|stroke (colours; default: the kind's), recorded?: the item as it was when used (recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} graphic: place a copy centred on `center`, its resources pasted along, selected, one undo step; colours: paint the selection (and the defaults) as paint.setFill/paint.setStroke; charStyle/paraStyle: add the style to the document (a name taken by different attributes gets a number) and apply it to the selected text, one undo step → {kind, ids?, style?}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Library Item
vectorcraft.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name)} delete an item (out of its group too) → null

vectorcraft.label: New Library Group
vectorcraft.params: {library?, name?: "Group" (a name the library's groups have, ignoring case, gets a number), items?: [{kind, item}] (moved into it out of their groups)} a new group of items, after the others → {library, group: its name}

vectorcraft.label: Rename Library Group
vectorcraft.params: {library?, group: name, name} rename a group (another group's name, ignoring case, is an error) → {library, group: the new name}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Library Group
vectorcraft.params: {library?, group: name} delete a group: its items stay in the library, ungrouped → {library, ungrouped: how many}

vectorcraft.label: Move Library Item to Group
vectorcraft.params: {library?, kind, item: name (graphic: id or name), group?: name (null or none: out of its group), before?: item | after?: item (an item of the same kind, named as `item` is)} put an item in a group (out of the one it was in); with `before` or `after`, also move it just before or after that item in the order its kind is shown in, as dragging it in the Libraries panel does → {library, kind, item, group: name or null}

vectorcraft.label: Move Library Group
vectorcraft.params: {library?, group: name, to: index} move a group to position `to` of the library's groups (0 = first; past the end: last), as dragging its header in the Libraries panel does → {library, group, to: where it went}

vectorcraft.label: Export Library
vectorcraft.params: {library?: id or name (default: the current library), path?} write a library (its colours, styles, graphics with their art and thumbnails, and groups) as a .vclibrary file (JSON, as libraries are kept) → {path, name}; without path → {data: the file's text, name}

vectorcraft.label: Import Library
vectorcraft.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: the library's name (default: the file's)} add the library of a .vclibrary file (as library.export writes) as a new library, made the current one; a name another library has gets a number (`Brand (2)`) → {id, name, graphics, colors, charStyles, paraStyles, groups (counts)}

vectorcraft.label: Expand…
vectorcraft.params: {object?: true (type → outlines, live shapes → paths, effects baked, blends → groups of their steps, repeats → groups of their instances, Intertwine groups → groups of their objects and of the parts drawn over the others (clip groups), envelopes → their distorted content, placed documents → editable copies of their art, as placing the file without link gives, its symbols, patterns, swatches and images joining the document), fill?: true (gradient fills → `gradient` art, pattern fills → their tiles in a clip group shaped like the object), stroke?: true (strokes → filled outlines), gradient?: "objects" (default: `steps` solid strips, concentric ellipses for radial gradients) | "mesh" (a gradient mesh); both in a clip group shaped like the object (freeform gradients always become a mesh shaped like it), steps?: 1..1000 (255)} one undo step → {ids}

vectorcraft.label: Expand Options
vectorcraft.params: {} what each Expand option would change in the selection → {object, fill, stroke, gradient} (true: something to expand; gradient: a gradient fill that Fill expands, which Expand Gradient To applies to)

vectorcraft.label: Attributes
vectorcraft.params: {overprintFill?: bool, overprintStroke?: bool (aimed as object.setOverprint's fill and stroke, item? too), showCenter?: bool (the canvas shows the selected object's centre point), imageMap?: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url?: string ("" removes it; SVG export links the object), note?: string, ids?|id?, item?: appearance item index|null, target?: "object"|"contents"} set the Attributes panel's values on ids or the selection, as one undo step; a URL given joins the recent URLs (attributes.info) → {changed: objects}

vectorcraft.label: Fill Rule
vectorcraft.params: {rule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd", ids?|id?} the fill rule of the paths and compound paths in ids or the selection (groups: those inside), as one undo step → {changed}

vectorcraft.label: SVG Interactivity
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} → {ids, events: [{event, script}…] in the panel's order | null (the objects' events differ), files: [the linked JavaScript files…], eventNames: [the events the panel lists…]} the SVG Interactivity panel's values for ids or the selection

vectorcraft.label: Add Event
vectorcraft.params: {event: "onclick"|"onmouseover"|… (svgInteractivity.info's eventNames), script: string (the JavaScript; "" removes the event), ids?|id?} set the JavaScript an event runs on ids or the selection, replacing the event's script where it has one, as one undo step; SVG export writes it as the event attribute → {changed: objects}

vectorcraft.label: Remove Selected Entry
vectorcraft.params: {event, ids?|id?} remove an event and its JavaScript from ids or the selection, as one undo step → {changed: objects}

vectorcraft.label: Clear Events
vectorcraft.params: {ids?|id?} remove every event from ids or the selection, as one undo step → {changed: objects}

vectorcraft.label: Add JavaScript File
vectorcraft.params: {file: path or URL (written as given, without surrounding spaces)} link a JavaScript file to the document, after the others: SVG export writes a <script xlink:href> for each linked file. A file already linked stays where it is; a document links at most 64 files → {files}

vectorcraft.label: Remove JavaScript File
vectorcraft.params: {file} unlink a JavaScript file from the document → {files}

vectorcraft.label: New Art Has Basic Appearance
vectorcraft.params: {on?: bool (omitted: toggle)} the Appearance panel option (the preference newArtBasic, on by default): on, new art takes one fill and stroke (with the Stroke panel's options); off, the whole appearance of the last selected object (every fill, stroke and effect, opacity and blend mode) → {on}

vectorcraft.label: New Art Appearance
vectorcraft.params: {} what the next object drawn gets → {basic: New Art Has Basic Appearance, appearance: {items, effects} (the model's JSON; placed gradients relative to the unit box), opacity: 0..100, blend, graphicStyle: the style it is linked to or null, inherited: taken from the last selection}

vectorcraft.label: Color Themes
vectorcraft.params: {} the saved colour themes, in order → {themes: [{name, colors: ["#rrggbb"], keys: [colour keys, exact in each colour's model], rule?}]}

vectorcraft.label: Save Theme
vectorcraft.params: {colors: [1–5 colours] | color + rule (a harmony rule id or label, see color.harmony: its 5-colour theme from that base colour, base first), rule?: the rule it was made with, name?: (default "Theme N"), replace?: a saved theme's name (overwrite that theme in place, e.g. after editing it; it may be renamed), color?: one colour (as colors: [colour])} save a colour theme to the local theme library (the preferences) → {name, count: themes saved}

vectorcraft.label: Delete Theme
vectorcraft.params: {name} delete a saved colour theme → {deleted}

vectorcraft.label: Add to Swatches
